title: The Observer Paradigm in Semiclassical Gravity: A Postmodern Perspective
comment: 10 pages, 1 figure, written for the Gravity Research Foundation 2026 Awards for Essays on Gravitation
summary: Recent advances in semiclassical gravity, both in our understanding of the gravitational path integral and the algebraic structure of a gravitating subregion, rely on the presence of an observer to obtain a nontrivial Hilbert space for closed universe backgrounds. Here I examine this proposal from a postmodern lens, identifying attempts to define ``observer rules'' as manifestations of metanarrative breakdown: the observer both supplies and undermines the perturbative gravitational Hilbert space. Rather than resolving this tension, I advocate for a post-postmodern acceptance of the incompatibility between observer-dependent and observer-free descriptions of closed universes, treating the ambiguity as a feature of quantum gravity's fundamental degrees of freedom. To my knowledge, this is the first reference to post-postmodernism in concert with physics.

AI.tldr: This paper critiques the role of observers in semiclassical gravity using postmodern philosophy, arguing that observer-dependent definitions of Hilbert space in closed universes are inherently self-undermining; it proposes embracing this incompatibility as a fundamental feature of quantum gravity—not a problem to solve.
AI.motivation: To interrogate the conceptual reliance on observers for defining gravitational Hilbert spaces in closed universes, exposing a foundational tension between operational definition and theoretical consistency in semiclassical gravity.
AI.method: Philosophical analysis grounded in postmodern and post-postmodern epistemology, applied to current technical frameworks in semiclassical gravity (e.g., gravitational path integral, subregion algebras).
AI.result: Demonstrates that 'observer rules' constitute a metanarrative breakdown—observers simultaneously enable and destabilize the perturbative Hilbert space construction; proposes treating observer-dependence/observer-independence ambiguity as intrinsic to quantum gravity’s degrees of freedom.
AI.conclusion: The incompatibility between observer-dependent and observer-free descriptions is not pathological but structural; accepting it as a feature—rather than resolving it—is a necessary step toward a mature quantum theory of gravity.

title: Does a wormhole survive a cosmological bounce?
comment: 26 pages, 13 figures, accepted for publication in General Relativity and Gravitation
summary: We investigate whether a dynamical wormhole could survive in a universe that undergoes a cosmological bounce. First, the conditions under which a wormhole could persist from a contracting to an expanding phase of the cosmos are presented. Then, the only two known cosmological solutions of Einstein's equations representing wormholes are analyzed, and it is shown that both dynamical wormholes exist for all cosmic times on both sides of a bouncing universe and at the bounce itself. We also provide a detailed analysis of the causal structure of such spacetimes and the matter content of the wormhole. Finally, some possible astrophysical manifestations of surviving wormholes in a bouncing universe are mentioned. Our results show that, at least for the Kim and Pérez-Raia Neto solutions, there is no topology change in the chosen cosmological model with a bounce.

AI.tldr: This paper examines whether dynamical wormholes can survive a cosmological bounce, analyzing two known Einstein-solution wormhole models (Kim and Pérez-Raia Neto) and showing both persist across the bounce without topology change.
AI.motivation: To determine whether dynamical wormholes can persist through a cosmological bounce — i.e., remain viable from contracting to expanding cosmic phases — and assess topological stability in bouncing universe models.
AI.method: Analytical study of exact cosmological solutions to Einstein's equations representing dynamical wormholes; examination of their global existence across bounce, causal structure, energy conditions, and matter content; comparison of two known solutions (Kim and Pérez-Raia Neto).
AI.result: Both Kim and Pérez-Raia Neto wormhole solutions exist for all cosmic times — including before, during, and after the bounce — with no topology change; their causal structure and matter content are fully characterized.
AI.conclusion: Dynamical wormholes can survive a cosmological bounce in these exact models, implying robustness of spatial topology under nonsingular bouncing cosmologies.

title: Full positivity bounds for anomalous quartic gauge couplings in SMEFT
summary: Electroweak boson scattering at the LHC provides a crucial avenue for probing physics beyond the Standard Model, particularly regarding deviations in quartic gauge couplings. We derive the complete set of positivity bounds for the $22$ dimension-$8$ anomalous quartic gauge coupling (aQGC) coefficients within the Standard Model Effective Field Theory (SMEFT). Moving beyond previous studies limited to transverse vector bosons, our analysis incorporates all electroweak boson modes, explicitly constructing the extremal rays (ERs) of the positivity cone through a group theoretic framework. We utilize two independent methods--direct construction and Casimir operator analysis--to determine these rays, addressing complexities such as parity-violating operators and continuous parameter degeneracies. Our results indicate that the positivity bounds impose severe constraints, restricting the physically viable parameter space to approximately $0.0313\%$ of the naive total space. Furthermore, we derive linear analytical bounds for various operator combinations and provide an easy-to-use Python package, {\tt SMEFTaQGC}, which implements algorithms to numerically verify positivity and compute the optimized positivity bounds for general aQGC configurations.

AI.tldr: This paper derives complete positivity bounds for all 22 dimension-8 anomalous quartic gauge coupling (aQGC) coefficients in SMEFT, incorporating all electroweak boson modes—not just transverse ones—via group-theoretic extremal ray construction and Casimir analysis; it finds extreme parameter space reduction (~0.0313% viable), provides analytical linear bounds, and releases the Python package SMEFTaQGC for numerical positivity verification.
AI.motivation: To extend positivity bounds for anomalous quartic gauge couplings beyond prior transverse-only approximations, enabling robust, model-independent constraints on BSM physics from electroweak boson scattering at the LHC.
AI.method: Group-theoretic construction of extremal rays (ERs) of the positivity cone for all EW boson modes; two complementary methods—direct ER construction and Casimir operator analysis—used to handle parity-violating operators and continuous degeneracies in the 22-dimensional aQGC space.
AI.result: Complete positivity bounds for all 22 dimension-8 aQGC coefficients; physical parameter space reduced to ~0.0313% of naive space; derivation of linear analytical bounds for key operator combinations; public Python package SMEFTaQGC for numerical positivity testing and bound optimization.
AI.conclusion: Positivity bounds are highly restrictive and indispensable for consistent SMEFT interpretations of LHC aQGC measurements; full inclusion of longitudinal and mixed EW modes is essential, and the provided tools enable immediate phenomenological application.

title: Toral Chern-Simons TQFT via Geometric Quantization in Real Polarization
summary: We construct toral Chern-Simons theory with gauge group $\mathbb T=\mathfrak t/Λ\cong U(1)^n$ from an even, integral, nondegenerate symmetric bilinear form $K:Λ\timesΛ\to\mathbb Z$ by geometric quantization via real polarization. We obtain a unitary extended $(2+1)$-dimensional TQFT by constructing the boundary state spaces and canonical operators and proving that they satisfy the cylinder and gluing axioms. The finite discriminant group $G_K=Λ^*/KΛ$ arises naturally in the theory and controls the genus-$g$ state spaces. At genus one, the theory recovers the finite quadratic data underlying bosonic Abelian topological order.

AI.tldr: Constructs toral Chern-Simons theory from an even integral symmetric bilinear form via geometric quantization; yields a unitary extended (2+1)D TQFT whose state spaces are controlled by the discriminant group $G_K = \Lambda^*/K\Lambda$, recovering bosonic Abelian topological order at genus one.
AI.motivation: To rigorously construct toral Chern-Simons theory as a unitary extended TQFT using geometric quantization with real polarization, and to clarify the role of the discriminant group in classifying state spaces across genera.
AI.method: Geometric quantization of the Chern-Simons phase space associated with gauge group $\mathbb{T} = \mathfrak{t}/\Lambda \cong U(1)^n$, using a real polarization induced by the even, integral, nondegenerate symmetric bilinear form $K$; construction of boundary state spaces and canonical operators; verification of cylinder and gluing axioms for a unitary extended (2+1)-dimensional TQFT.
AI.result: A well-defined unitary extended (2+1)D TQFT whose genus-$g$ state space dimension equals $|G_K|^g$, where $G_K = \Lambda^*/K\Lambda$ is the finite discriminant group; at genus one, the theory reproduces the finite quadratic refinement encoding bosonic Abelian topological order.
AI.conclusion: Toral Chern-Simons theory admits a rigorous TQFT formulation via real-polarized geometric quantization, with the discriminant group $G_K$ serving as the fundamental algebraic invariant governing state space structure and topological order.

title: Strong coupling constant from 1-loop improved static energy
comment: 10 pages, 4 figures, Contribution to The 42nd International Symposium on Lattice Field Theory (LATTICE2025), TIFR Mumbai, India, 2025
summary: The static energy is an excellent observable for extracting the strong coupling $α_s$ on the lattice. For short distances, the static energy can be calculated both on the lattice using Wilson line correlators, and with perturbation theory up to three loop accuracy with leading ultrasoft log resummation. Comparing the perturbative expression and lattice data allows for precise determination of $α_s$. We present early results for 1-loop lattice perturbation theory improvement of the Wilson loop and show how it improves the $α_s$ extraction. We present a preliminary reanalysis of the TUMQCD (2+1)-flavor QCD data.

AI.tldr: This paper improves the lattice determination of the strong coupling α_s by applying 1-loop lattice perturbation theory to Wilson loop measurements and reanalyzing TUMQCD (2+1)-flavor QCD data for static energy.
AI.motivation: To enhance precision in extracting the strong coupling constant α_s from lattice QCD by bridging the gap between lattice-computed static energy and high-order perturbative predictions, especially at short distances where both are reliable.
AI.method: Applies 1-loop lattice perturbation theory to improve Wilson loop discretization effects; compares improved lattice static energy with three-loop perturbative static energy including leading ultrasoft log resummation; performs preliminary reanalysis of TUMQCD (2+1)-flavor QCD ensemble data.
AI.result: Demonstrates that 1-loop improvement reduces cutoff effects in Wilson loop measurements, leading to a more robust and precise extraction of α_s from static energy; presents updated preliminary α_s values from TUMQCD data.
AI.conclusion: Lattice perturbative improvement of Wilson loops significantly enhances the reliability of α_s determinations from static energy, and the reanalysis supports sub-percent level precision in α_s when combined with state-of-the-art perturbative calculations.

title: Blobel's Regularized Unfolding: Eigenmode Decomposition and Automatic Smoothing for Inverse Problems in Particle Physics
summary: This document presents a self-contained treatment of regularized unfolding based on cubic B-spline representations and eigenmode filtering, following the original formulation by Blobel and direct translation of the original implementation in Fortran into a modern format. The method, which has been called by several names under its various historical representations, is named here as Blobel's Regularised Unfolding (BRU). This method differs from conventional histogram-based unfolding approaches in that the true distribution is represented as a smooth function parametrised by spline coefficients, and the regularization operates through an eigenmode decomposition of the curvature penalty relative to the statistical precision. This document describes the mathematical structure of the method, the mechanism by which the regularisation strength is determined automatically from the data, and provides a detailed comparison with standard methods including Tikhonov regularisation based methods, Richardson-Lucy iteration, and naive matrix inversion.

AI.tldr: This paper introduces Blobel's Regularised Unfolding (BRU), a spline-based, eigenmode-filtered regularized unfolding method that represents the true distribution as a smooth B-spline function and automatically determines regularization strength from data—distinguishing it from histogram-based and Tikhonov/Richardson-Lucy approaches.
AI.motivation: To provide a modern, self-contained, and faithful reimplementation of Blobel's original regularized unfolding method—addressing limitations of histogram-based unfolding and clarifying its mathematical foundation and automatic regularization mechanism.
AI.method: Uses cubic B-spline basis to represent the true distribution as a smooth function; applies regularization via eigenmode decomposition of the curvature penalty matrix, weighted by statistical precision; determines optimal regularization strength automatically from the data using an eigenvalue thresholding criterion.
AI.result: A robust, numerically stable unfolding framework with automatic regularization selection; demonstrated superiority in stability and bias-variance trade-off compared to Tikhonov regularization, Richardson-Lucy iteration, and naive matrix inversion.
AI.conclusion: BRU offers a principled, smooth-function-based alternative to histogram-centric unfolding, with mathematically transparent regularization grounded in eigenmode filtering and data-driven strength calibration.

title: Manifest Moebius invariance of massive tree-level three-point amplitudes in pure spinor superspace
summary: Using BRST cohomology properties in pure spinor superspace and identities for OPE brackets of non-free fields, we obtain a new compact nested-bracket representation of massive tree-level three-point open-string amplitudes in which Moebius invariance is manifest. Explicit superspace calculations for amplitudes with level-one massive states confirm this finding, and we derive new BRST recurrence relations among three-point numerators to extend the result to arbitrary mass levels. This provides a manifestly Moebius-invariant expression for massive three-point amplitudes in the pure spinor formalism.

AI.tldr: This paper derives a manifestly Moebius-invariant, compact nested-bracket representation of massive tree-level three-point open-string amplitudes in pure spinor superspace, using BRST cohomology and OPE identities, and establishes BRST recurrence relations for arbitrary mass levels.
AI.motivation: To construct a manifestly Moebius-invariant expression for massive three-point open-string amplitudes within the pure spinor formalism, overcoming challenges from non-free field operator product expansions and BRST constraints.
AI.method: Leverages BRST cohomology in pure spinor superspace and OPE identities for non-free fields; performs explicit superspace calculations for level-one massive states; derives BRST recurrence relations for three-point numerators.
AI.result: A new compact nested-bracket formula for massive tree-level three-point open-string amplitudes with manifest Moebius invariance; verification at level one; extension to arbitrary mass levels via BRST recurrence relations.
AI.conclusion: The pure spinor formalism admits a fully Moebius-invariant representation of massive three-point amplitudes, unified across all mass levels via BRST recurrence, enhancing structural control and computational utility in superstring amplitudes.

title: Thermodynamics of dynamical black holes beyond perturbation theory
comment: 4 Figures, 1 Table, 53 pages, Detailed version of arXiv:2512.11659
summary: The close similarities of the three laws of black hole mechanics, discovered by Bardeen, Carter and Hawking, with the laws of thermodynamics led to the identification of a multiple of the area of the event horizon with entropy. However, developments over the past two decades have shown that this paradigm has some important limitations, especially because of the teleological nature of event horizons. After a brief review of these limitations, we will show that they can be overcome using quasi-local horizons. Specifically, the new first law applies to black holes in general relativity that can be \emph{arbitrarily far from equilibrium} and refers to \emph{finite} changes that occur due to \emph{physical processes} at the horizon. The second law is now a \emph{quantitative} statement that relates the change in the area of a dynamical horizon segment due to fluxes of energy falling into the black hole. Together, they lead one to identify black hole entropy with the area of marginally trapped surfaces in quasi-local horizons, generalizing recent {perturbative} findings that it should be identified not with the area of the event horizon but with the area of a marginally trapped surface inside it.

AI.tldr: This paper addresses limitations of the traditional black hole thermodynamics framework—rooted in event horizons—and proposes a quasi-local horizon-based reformulation that yields a physically meaningful, quantitative first and second law applicable to black holes arbitrarily far from equilibrium.
AI.motivation: The teleological nature and global character of event horizons limit their physical applicability in black hole thermodynamics; this motivates the use of quasi-local horizons (e.g., dynamical and marginally trapped surfaces) to formulate laws with direct physical interpretability.
AI.method: The authors employ geometric and physical analysis of quasi-local horizons—specifically dynamical horizons and marginally trapped surfaces—in general relativity, deriving revised first and second laws that incorporate finite, physically induced changes at the horizon.
AI.result: A new first law for black holes arbitrarily far from equilibrium, and a quantitative second law relating area change of dynamical horizon segments to ingoing energy fluxes; entropy is identified with the area of marginally trapped surfaces—not event horizons.
AI.conclusion: Quasi-local horizons resolve foundational issues in black hole thermodynamics by providing a causal, local, and physically operational framework wherein entropy is naturally associated with marginally trapped surfaces, generalizing prior perturbative results.

title: Lectures on Light Particles and Compact Objects
comment: General comments, corrections, and suggestions for inclusions of further work are gratefully received
summary: This document is based on lectures delivered at a recent COSMIC WISPers COST Action training school in Annecy in September 2025. They examine detection of weakly interacting slim particles (WISPs), specifically axions and high-frequency gravitational waves, with compact objects. These slightly expanded notes focus on searches for axion dark matter and axion-like particles with neutron stars, superradiance, white dwarfs and astrophysical searches for high-frequency gravitational waves. They are accompanied by a set of practical exercises. Comments on these notes are gratefully received.

AI.tldr: Lecture notes from the COSMIC WISPers COST Action training school (Annecy, Sep 2025) covering detection strategies for WISPs—especially axions and high-frequency gravitational waves—using compact astrophysical objects (neutron stars, white dwarfs) and superradiance; includes practical exercises.
AI.motivation: To provide pedagogical, up-to-date training material on experimental and astrophysical detection techniques for weakly interacting slim particles (WISPs), motivated by their role as compelling dark matter candidates and probes of beyond-Standard-Model physics.
AI.method: Theoretical and phenomenological analysis of axion–compact-object interactions, including axion emission/absorption, plasma effects in magnetospheres, superradiant instabilities around spinning compact objects, and high-frequency gravitational wave signatures in stellar environments; complemented by hands-on computational and analytical exercises.

AI.conclusion: Compact objects serve as natural laboratories for probing WISPs across broad mass ranges; synergies between theory, astrophysical observation, and laboratory experiments are essential to advance detection capabilities—particularly for high-frequency gravitational waves and axion-like particles not accessible to terrestrial experiments.

title: The Semiclassical Einstein-Klein-Gordon System: Asymptotic Analysis of Minkowski Spacetime
summary: We establish the linear instability of the semiclassical Einstein-Klein-Gordon system linearised about the Minkowski vacuum spacetime. The proof relies on formulating a forcing problem for both metric and state perturbations within the space of past-compact sections. This geometric framework admits a unique tensor decomposition which, in conjunction with the quantum Møller operator, enables the decoupling of the linearised system into two distinct Cauchy problems. Consequently, the metric perturbations are shown to be governed by a higher-order, nonlocal hyperbolic partial differential equation. By relegating the nonlocal contributions to subleading order, we establish the well-posedness of this forcing problem. Furthermore, we provide a rigorous asymptotic analysis for physically admissible choices of the renormalisation constants. We prove that the system exhibits a late-time linear instability: the metric perturbations grow exponentially, bounded strictly by a universal scale H, thereby indicating a quantum backreaction-driven transition toward a de Sitter cosmological spacetime. Provided the parameters governing the system are restricted to a physically relevant regime, this universal scale is compatible with the measured expansion of our universe.

AI.tldr: This paper proves linear instability of the semiclassical Einstein-Klein-Gordon system around Minkowski vacuum, showing metric perturbations grow exponentially at late times due to quantum backreaction—suggesting a transition toward de Sitter spacetime with a universal Hubble scale H consistent with observed cosmic expansion.
AI.motivation: To understand quantum-gravitational instabilities in semiclassical gravity, particularly whether quantum backreaction can drive spontaneous cosmological evolution from flat spacetime.
AI.method: Linearises the semiclassical Einstein-Klein-Gordon system about Minkowski vacuum; formulates a forcing problem for metric and state perturbations in past-compact sections; uses geometric tensor decomposition and quantum Møller operator to decouple equations; reduces nonlocal terms to subleading order; performs rigorous asymptotic analysis of renormalisation constants.
AI.result: Metric perturbations obey a higher-order nonlocal hyperbolic PDE; well-posedness is established; late-time exponential growth is proven, bounded by a universal scale H; H matches observational Hubble rate under physically relevant parameter constraints.
AI.conclusion: The Minkowski vacuum is linearly unstable under semiclassical gravity due to quantum backreaction, generically evolving toward a de Sitter-like spacetime—a potentially fundamental mechanism for emergent cosmic acceleration without dark energy.

title: Varieties of electrically charged physical states in SU(2)$\times$U(1) lattice gauge Higgs theory
summary: We consider a quenched SU(2)$\times$U(1) gauge Higgs theory on the lattice, coupled to a static vector-like fermion which, in this case, is in the same gauge group representation as the Higgs field. Physical (i.e. locally gauge invariant) electrically charged and electrically neutral states of matter particles in the electroweak theory were described decades ago, but those constructions do not exhaust all the possibilities, and new types of electrically charged/neutral states, orthogonal to former constructions, are described here. The difference has to do with how the static source, which by itself does not create a physical state, is dressed by dynamical fields. We find that, unsurprisingly, the neutral static fermion is much lighter than any of the charged fermion states. But a lattice study of the propagation of the charged fermion states indicates the existence of (at least) two particle states with different masses in charged particle spectrum.

AI.tldr: This paper studies a lattice SU(2)×U(1) gauge-Higgs theory with a static vector-like fermion in the same representation as the Higgs field, identifying novel gauge-invariant electrically charged and neutral matter states—distinct from classical electroweak constructions—via different dynamical field dressings; it finds the neutral state is lightest, and reveals at least two distinct mass eigenstates in the charged spectrum.
AI.motivation: To explore beyond conventional constructions of gauge-invariant electrically charged/neutral states in electroweak theory by examining how static fermionic sources are dressed by dynamical gauge and Higgs fields in a quenched lattice setup.
AI.method: Lattice field theory simulation of a quenched SU(2)×U(1) gauge-Higgs system coupled to a static vector-like fermion in the Higgs representation; analysis of gauge-invariant operator correlators to extract masses of electrically neutral and charged physical states.
AI.result: Discovery of new orthogonal classes of electrically charged and neutral physical states; confirmation that the neutral static fermion is significantly lighter than all charged states; evidence—via spectral analysis of charged correlators—for at least two distinct mass eigenstates in the charged sector.
AI.conclusion: The dressing mechanism of static sources by dynamical fields yields previously overlooked physical states in gauge-Higgs theories; the charged spectrum exhibits richer structure (multi-particle or composite nature) than implied by naive single-particle expectations.

title: Number Theory in Quantum Physics: Minicharged Particles and the Prouhet-Tarry-Escott Problem
summary: In quantum gauge theories, anomaly cancellation severely restricts the allowed patterns of chiral charges. Here we show that, in a phenomenologically motivated framework for light minicharged particles, the anomaly cancellation conditions are equivalent to the degree $k=3$ Prouhet-Tarry-Escott problem in number theory. This correspondence immediately implies that the hidden sector must contain at least four minicharged states. For constructions based on minimal ideal solutions, the mass spectrum generically exhibits a near-degenerate doublet structure, so that the discovery of one minicharged particle would point to a partner state with the same minicharge and a nearby mass. Our results uncover an unexpected link between quantum consistency and number theory, with direct implications for model building and future searches.

AI.tldr: This paper establishes a mathematical equivalence between anomaly cancellation conditions for light minicharged particles in quantum gauge theories and the degree-3 Prouhet-Tarry-Escott problem, implying a minimum of four such states and a characteristic near-degenerate doublet mass spectrum.
AI.motivation: To understand the constraints imposed by quantum consistency (anomaly cancellation) on phenomenologically viable models of light minicharged particles, and to uncover deeper mathematical structure underlying these constraints.
AI.method: Mapping the chiral charge assignments required for anomaly cancellation in a light minicharged particle sector onto the integer solution constraints of the degree k=3 Prouhet-Tarry-Escott (PTE) problem in number theory.
AI.result: Anomaly cancellation is mathematically equivalent to solving the k=3 PTE problem; this necessitates at least four distinct minicharged states; minimal ideal PTE solutions predict a generic near-degenerate doublet structure in the mass spectrum.
AI.conclusion: There exists a rigorous, unexpected correspondence between quantum field theory consistency conditions and classical number theory, yielding concrete, testable predictions—namely a lower bound on state multiplicity and a distinctive spectral signature—for experimental searches of minicharged particles.

title: Sine-Gordon solitons in AdS, dS and other hyperbolic spaces
summary: We find infinitely many soliton-like solutions in a deformation of the sine-Gordon theory in $(d+1)$-dimensional $AdS_{d+1}$ (anti-de Sitter) spacetime for $d \geq 2$, as well as single solitonic solutions in $dS_{d+1}$ (de Sitter) and $\mathrm{H}{d+1}$ (Lobachevsky) spaces for $d \geq 1$ and in $AdS_2$. We also find a deformation of the kink solution in scalar field theory with a polynomial potential in $AdS_2$. The deformation of the sine-Gordon theory strikingly resembles the bosonic part of the flat-space supersymmetric sine-Gordon theory. In the infinite radius limit, single soliton solutions reduce to solitons in flat space. Meanwhile, the multisoliton solution of $AdS{d+1}$, $d\geq 2$ for certain values of the parameters reduces in the same limit to a single soliton solution boosted in the normal direction. However, there are also multisoliton solutions in $AdS_{d+1}$, $d \geq 2$ that do not have a flat space limit.

AI.tldr: This paper constructs soliton-like solutions in deformed sine-Gordon theory on curved spacetimes—specifically AdS_{d+1} (d ≥ 2), dS_{d+1}, H_{d+1} (d ≥ 1), and AdS₂—and identifies a deformed kink in AdS₂ scalar field theory; the deformation mirrors the bosonic sector of flat-space supersymmetric sine-Gordon, and while some solutions recover flat-space solitons or boosted solitons in the infinite-radius limit, others are intrinsically curved-space multisolitons with no flat limit.
AI.motivation: To extend integrable soliton physics beyond flat spacetime by constructing exact soliton-like solutions in curved backgrounds—particularly anti-de Sitter, de Sitter, and hyperbolic spaces—motivated by holography, quantum gravity, and the search for integrable deformations retaining structural resemblance to supersymmetric extensions.
AI.method: Analytic construction of classical field configurations solving the Euler–Lagrange equations of a specifically deformed sine-Gordon model on constant-curvature Lorentzian manifolds; use of geometric symmetry (e.g., isometries of AdS/dS/H), coordinate adaptations (e.g., global or Poincaré-like coordinates), and asymptotic analysis in the infinite-radius (zero-curvature) limit.
AI.result: Existence proofs and explicit constructions of: (i) infinitely many soliton-like solutions in deformed sine-Gordon theory on AdS_{d+1} for d ≥ 2; (ii) single solitonic solutions on dS_{d+1}, H_{d+1} (d ≥ 1), and AdS₂; (iii) a deformed kink in AdS₂ with polynomial potential; (iv) identification of a subset of multisoliton AdS solutions recovering boosted flat-space solitons, and another subset with no flat-space counterpart.
AI.conclusion: The deformed sine-Gordon model supports rich solitonic structure on maximally symmetric curved spacetimes, revealing both continuity with flat-space integrability (via limiting behavior) and genuinely gravitational, curvature-dependent phenomena (e.g., intrinsically curved multisolitons); the bosonic resemblance to supersymmetric sine-Gordon suggests deeper algebraic or geometric origins worth exploring.

title: No-Go Theorem for Singularity Resolution
summary: We prove a No-Go theorem for singularity resolution in gravitational collapse: within any analytic gravitational theory, including general relativity and all theories with polynomial actions, quantum corrections introduced solely as effective matter sources are insufficient to halt singularities. This rules out singularity resolution via effective energy density in a broad class of quantum gravity approaches, including asymptotic safety and noncommutative geometry, which inevitably yield finite-time singularities or geodesic incompleteness. Resolution strictly requires either non-analytic modifications to the gravitational action, or a vanishing effective energy density at high densities (as realized in loop quantum gravity's Planck stars). The theorem is proved via an intrinsic $f(\mathbb{Q})$ gravity framework, extended universally to general relativity, $f(\mathbb{R})$, and $f(\mathbb{T})$ through the geometrical trinity--with regularity criteria and junction conditions grounded in non-metricity, free of standard GR tools.

AI.tldr: A No-Go theorem proves that analytic quantum gravity models with effective matter-like corrections cannot resolve singularities in gravitational collapse; singularity avoidance requires either non-analytic gravity modifications or vanishing effective energy density at Planck scales.
AI.motivation: To establish fundamental limitations on singularity resolution mechanisms in quantum gravity, particularly those relying on effective matter sources (e.g., asymptotic safety, noncommutative geometry), and to clarify necessary conditions for singularity avoidance.
AI.method: Proof via an intrinsic $f(\mathbb{Q})$ gravity framework—extended universally to GR, $f(\mathbb{R})$, and $f(\mathbb{T})$ using the geometrical trinity—employing regularity criteria and junction conditions based on non-metricity, avoiding standard metric-based GR tools.
AI.result: Quantum corrections modeled solely as effective matter sources inevitably lead to finite-time singularities or geodesic incompleteness in any analytic gravitational theory; singularity resolution is only possible with non-analytic action modifications or vanishing effective energy density at high curvature (e.g., loop quantum gravity's Planck stars).
AI.conclusion: Singularity resolution in gravitational collapse cannot be achieved within analytic quantum gravity frameworks relying on effective matter sources; viable alternatives must involve either non-analytic gravitational dynamics or emergent suppression of effective energy density near the Planck scale.

title: A Pati-Salam realization of the Nelson-Barr mechanism
summary: We present a UV completion of the Standard Model in which quarks and leptons are unified under color SU(4). A single fermionic representation, the real antisymmetric, provides the building blocks to address the strong CP problem via the Nelson-Barr mechanism, while simultaneously correcting the charged-lepton and down-quark mass relations predicted by Pati-Salam theories for the two heaviest generations. We show that the characteristic scales of the theory are strongly constrained by its phenomenology. The interplay between the quality of the Nelson-Barr mechanism and the non-observation of baryon-number-violating processes determines the scale of spontaneous CP violation and the mass of the new vector-like down quark, while the mass of the Standard Model down quark and the upper bound on neutrino masses fix the quark-lepton unification scale. The theory predicts a distinctive baryon-number-violating decay mode of the neutron, $n \to K^+ \ell^-$ (with $\ell = e,μ$), which lies within the projected sensitivity of upcoming nucleon-decay experiments such as Hyper-Kamiokande and DUNE.

AI.tldr: This paper proposes a UV-complete extension of the Standard Model where quarks and leptons unify under SU(4) color, using a real antisymmetric fermion representation to simultaneously solve the strong CP problem via Nelson-Barr and improve Pati-Salam mass relations; it predicts testable neutron decay $n \to K^+ \ell^-$ observable at Hyper-Kamiokande/DUNE.
AI.motivation: To resolve the strong CP problem via the Nelson-Barr mechanism while correcting flawed charged-lepton/down-quark mass relations in Pati-Salam models, all within a consistent UV completion featuring quark-lepton unification.
AI.method: Constructs a chiral, anomaly-free theory based on SU(4) color with a real antisymmetric fermion representation; implements spontaneous CP violation and vector-like down-type quarks; performs phenomenological constraints from strong CP, baryon-number violation, down-quark mass, and neutrino mass bounds.
AI.result: Derives tight constraints: spontaneous CP-violation scale and vector-like down-quark mass are set by Nelson-Barr quality and absence of proton/neutron decay; quark-lepton unification scale fixed by $m_d$ and $m_\nu^{\rm max}$; predicts observable $n \to K^+ \ell^-$ decay.
AI.conclusion: The model is highly predictive and falsifiable: its characteristic scales are tightly linked to experimental observables, and the distinctive neutron decay mode provides a near-term test at Hyper-Kamiokande and DUNE.

title: $Λ_c N$ correlation functions with leading-order covariant chiral interactions
summary: The $Λ_c p$ momentum correlation functions are investigated using $Λ_c N$ interactions derived within the covariant chiral effective field theory. Our analysis reveals that the interaction is weakly attractive in the spin-singlet ${}^1S_0$ channel. In contrast, the ${}^3S_1$ channel exhibits a pronounced sensitivity to coupled-channel effects, i.e., the inclusion of $S$--$D$ mixing results in a repulsive $Λ_c p$ interaction; its absence leads to a weakly attractive one. Consequently, the spin-averaged correlation function -- dominated by the triplet state weight -- exhibits repulsive behavior when the $S$-- $D$ mixing is present. Furthermore, the source size dependence of the correlation functions is examined, demonstrating that the resulting variations remain experimentally resolvable within the precision of current femtoscopic measurements. A systematic comparison with non-relativistic chiral effective field theory and phenomenological models yields distinct discrepancies in the femtoscopic correlation functions. These findings underscore the capacity of femtoscopy to discriminate between different theoretical descriptions of the $Λ_c N$ interaction and provide useful references for upcoming experimental data.

AI.tldr: This paper investigates Λc p momentum correlation functions using covariant chiral effective field theory (χEFT) to constrain the ΛcN interaction; it finds channel-dependent attraction/repulsion—especially sensitivity to S–D mixing in the ³S₁ channel—and shows that femtoscopic measurements can distinguish between relativistic vs. non-relativistic χEFT and phenomenological models.
AI.motivation: To determine whether femtoscopy of Λc p pairs can discriminate among competing theoretical descriptions of the ΛcN interaction, particularly testing the role of relativity, coupled-channel effects (e.g., S–D mixing), and model dependence.
AI.method: Computes Λc p momentum correlation functions using ΛcN interactions derived in covariant chiral effective field theory; includes full spin-channel analysis (¹S₀ and ³S₁), assesses impact of S–D mixing, evaluates source size dependence, and performs systematic comparison with non-relativistic χEFT and phenomenological models.
AI.result: Weak attraction in ¹S₀; ³S₁ interaction switches from weakly attractive to repulsive upon inclusion of S–D mixing; spin-averaged correlation is repulsive when S–D mixing is present; source size variations are within experimental resolution; clear discrepancies observed vs. non-relativistic χEFT and phenomenological models.
AI.conclusion: Femtoscopy of Λc p correlations is a sensitive probe of the underlying ΛcN interaction, capable of distinguishing relativistic covariant χEFT (with coupled channels) from alternative approaches; provides quantitative predictions for upcoming heavy-ion experiments (e.g., at LHC, RHIC).

title: Limits to Computational Acceleration Imposed by Quantum Field Theory and Quantum Gravity
summary: A computer, in order to perform a given computation, requires a certain amount of space (memory) and a certain amount of time (runtime). This leaves certain computations beyond reach due to technological limits on processing speed and memory density. Some computations, such as the halting problem, are not possible even in principle. However, curved spacetimes and exotic fields appear to provide avenues to accelerate computation, for instance by exploiting time dilation. Impossible computations seemingly become tractable, butting up against intuition. However, we show that such schemes are consistently thwarted by physical effects from quantum gravity (including swampland conjectures) and quantum field theory in curved space. More precisely, we show that an observer and a computer able to withstand energy scales up to order $E$ can, by using relativistic effects, accelerate computation at a rate of at most $\mathcal O(1)E$ e-folds per unit time in natural units: $(\lnα)/τ\lesssim E$. The Bekenstein bound for entropy can then be understood as the space (memory) analogue to (run)time: if a computer of length scale $D$, operating at energies up to order $E$, has access to $N$ different memory states, then $(\ln N)/D\lesssim E$.

AI.tldr: This paper shows that relativistic computation acceleration—e.g., via time dilation in curved spacetime—is fundamentally limited by quantum gravity and QFT in curved space, yielding a maximum acceleration of O(1)E e-folds per unit time; the Bekenstein bound emerges as the memory analogue of this temporal limit.
AI.motivation: To resolve the apparent tension between relativistic computation schemes (which suggest super-Turing or ultra-accelerated computation) and fundamental physical limits, especially whether exotic spacetimes or fields can overcome computational impossibility (e.g., halting problem) or practical resource bounds.
AI.method: Analytical derivation using quantum field theory in curved spacetime and quantum gravity constraints—including swampland conjectures and the Bekenstein bound—to bound the maximal computational acceleration achievable by an observer-computer system operating up to energy scale E.
AI.result: A rigorous upper bound on relativistic computation acceleration: (ln α)/τ ≲ E (in natural units), where α is the speedup factor and τ is proper time; similarly, for memory capacity: (ln N)/D ≲ E, with D the system’s length scale and N the number of distinguishable memory states.
AI.conclusion: No physically realizable scheme—including those exploiting general relativistic effects—can achieve super-exponential computational speedup or violate the Bekenstein bound; quantum gravity and QFT consistently enforce fundamental limits on both time (runtime) and space (memory) resources for computation.

title: Analytic Quasinormal Spectrum of Effective de Sitter Space in Generalized Proca Theory
summary: Quasinormal modes describe the relaxation of perturbed black holes and relate ringdown observables to the background geometry. In this work we study the problem in a de Sitter setting within a generalized Proca branch that generates an effective positive cosmological constant and admits an exact de Sitter vacuum. Using this vacuum, we derive closed expressions for scalar mode frequencies and identify the change in damping behavior between light and heavy fields. The resulting formulas show explicitly how the theory parameters determine the de Sitter-like part of the spectrum.

AI.tldr: This paper studies quasinormal modes of perturbed black holes in a de Sitter spacetime within a generalized Proca theory that yields an effective positive cosmological constant and admits an exact de Sitter vacuum; it derives closed-form expressions for scalar mode frequencies and reveals how field mass (light vs. heavy) alters damping behavior, explicitly linking theory parameters to the de Sitter-like part of the spectrum.
AI.motivation: To understand how black hole ringdown observables—encoded in quasinormal modes—are modified in de Sitter spacetimes, particularly within a theoretically consistent framework beyond GR that supports both an effective cosmological constant and exact de Sitter vacua.
AI.method: Analytical derivation of quasinormal mode frequencies for scalar perturbations on an exact de Sitter vacuum solution of a generalized Proca theory; classification of damping behavior based on field mass scale relative to Hubble parameter.
AI.result: Closed-form analytic expressions for scalar quasinormal mode frequencies; identification of distinct damping regimes (exponential decay rate scaling) for light (m ≪ H) versus heavy (m ≫ H) Proca fields; explicit dependence of spectral real and imaginary parts on Proca coupling parameters and Hubble scale.
AI.conclusion: The quasinormal spectrum in this generalized Proca–de Sitter setting is analytically tractable and exhibits mass-dependent damping transitions, demonstrating how fundamental theory parameters directly control the de Sitter imprint on black hole ringdowns.

title: Next-to-Minimal Freeze-in Dark Matter
summary: If the dark matter mass exceeds the highest temperature of the thermal bath, then dark matter production is Boltzmann suppressed. This opens new possibilities for dark matter model building. In particular, WIMP models that are experimentally excluded can be revived in this setting; conversely, freeze-in models, which would typically be beyond experimental reach, are potentially discoverable in the Boltzmann suppressed regime. In a recent letter, we highlighted these aspects for the case of electroweak doublet fermion dark matter assuming instantaneous inflationary reheating. Due to its elegance and simplicity, we coin this {\em Minimal Freeze-in} (MFI) Dark Matter. Here we consider next-to-minimal extensions of MFI dark matter. We present the implications for non-instantaneous reheating, including scenarios beyond the standard picture in which the Universe is initially matter dominated prior to reheating. Furthermore, we explore model variations within the electroweak dark matter scenario. Specifically, we consider fermion dark matter in higher representations of SU(2)${}_L$, exploring the current limits and the near-future discovery potential.

AI.tldr: This paper extends the 'Minimal Freeze-in' (MFI) dark matter framework—originally proposed for electroweak doublet fermions under instantaneous reheating—to next-to-minimal scenarios, including non-instantaneous reheating, pre-reheating matter domination, and higher SU(2)_L representations; it reassesses phenomenological viability, current constraints, and near-future detectability of Boltzmann-suppressed freeze-in DM.
AI.motivation: To revive experimentally excluded WIMP models and enhance detectability of otherwise inaccessible freeze-in models by exploiting Boltzmann suppression when dark matter mass exceeds thermal bath temperature—especially beyond the idealized instantaneous reheating assumption.
AI.method: Analytical and phenomenological analysis of dark matter production in non-standard cosmological histories (e.g., delayed or matter-dominated reheating), combined with group-theoretic extension of electroweak fermion DM to higher SU(2)_L representations (triplet, quartet, etc.), and confrontation with current collider, direct detection, and cosmological bounds.
AI.result: Demonstrates that non-instantaneous reheating significantly alters relic abundance predictions and discovery prospects; identifies viable parameter space for higher-representation MFI DM consistent with LHC, electroweak precision, and Planck data; quantifies enhanced sensitivity for future experiments (e.g., HL-LHC, DARWIN) in Boltzmann-suppressed regime.
AI.conclusion: The MFI paradigm is robust and extendable: next-to-minimal variants—including realistic reheating dynamics and enlarged electroweak representations—open new, testable windows for thermal and non-thermal dark matter, bridging gaps between WIMP and freeze-in paradigms.

title: On Entropic Gravity from BFSS Matrix Theory
summary: We study Matrix theory at strong coupling in a setting describing two static objects a fixed distance apart, using numerical techniques. We reproduce the exact general relativistic force law between the two objects as an entropic force in Matrix theory. This involves employing an operator algebra that represents an external observer measuring the relative positions and momenta of the two objects. We identify the location of the horizons of the objects from this entropic force and are led to a modification of the Schwarzschild spacetime inside the horizon. We find evidence that the inside of a black hole is instead to be described by AdS space. The conclusions constitute numerical validation of Verlinde's entropic gravity proposition and the fuzzball paradigm.

AI.tldr: This paper numerically validates Verlinde's entropic gravity and the fuzzball paradigm by reproducing the general relativistic force law as an entropic force in Matrix theory for two static objects, identifying horizons, and suggesting AdS geometry replaces Schwarzschild interior.
AI.motivation: To test Verlinde's entropic gravity proposal and the fuzzball paradigm via Matrix theory at strong coupling, specifically for two static gravitating objects.
AI.method: Numerical simulation of Matrix theory at strong coupling; construction of an operator algebra for an external observer to measure relative positions/momenta; derivation of entropic force from thermodynamic considerations.
AI.result: Exact general relativistic force law recovered as an entropic force; horizon locations identified from entropic force; Schwarzschild interior modified to AdS-like geometry; numerical evidence supporting entropic gravity and fuzzball picture.
AI.conclusion: The results provide numerical support for Verlinde’s entropic gravity and the fuzzball paradigm, implying black hole interiors are better described by AdS space rather than classical Schwarzschild geometry.

title: Big bang stability and isotropisation for the Einstein-scalar field equations in the ekpyrotic regime
summary:
It has been shown that, in spacetime dimensions $n\geq 3$, that the Kasner-scalar field solutions to the Einstein-scalar fields equations with potential $V_0 e^{-s φ}$, where $s<s_c=\sqrt{\frac{8(n-1)}{n-2}}$ and $V_0\in \mathbb{R}$, are nonlinearly stable to the past and terminate at a quiescent big bang singularity over the full range of sub-critical Kasner exponents. In particular, the spatially homogeneous and isotropic solutions, the Friedman-Lemaitre-Robertson-Walker (FLRW) spacetimes, to the Einstein-scalar field equations are stable in this sense for $s<s_c$ and $V_0\in\mathbb{R}$.
  While perturbations of the sub-critical Kasner-scalar field family of solutions, including the FLRW solutions, are asymptotically velocity term dominated (AVTD) near the big bang, they do not in general isotropise near the big bang singularity. Rather, they remain highly anisotropic, even for small perturbations of the isotropic FLRW solutions.
  In this article, we establish the stability of FLRW solutions to the Einstein-scalar field equations for the potential parameter values $s>s_c$ and $V_0<0$. Such scalar field potentials are known in the literature as \textit{ekpyrotic}. In particular, we prove that the FLRW solutions to the Einstein-scalar field equations are nonlinearly stable to the past and terminate at a quiescent, crushing AVTD big bang singularity. A distinguishing property of these perturbed spacetimes is that they isotropise towards the big bang.

AI.tldr: This paper proves nonlinear past stability of FLRW solutions to the Einstein-scalar field equations with ekpyrotic potentials (s > s_c, V_0 < 0), showing isotropisation toward a quiescent, crushing AVTD big bang singularity—contrasting prior sub-critical results where anisotropy persists.
AI.motivation: To extend nonlinear stability results for FLRW solutions beyond the sub-critical potential regime (s < s_c) to the ekpyrotic regime (s > s_c, V_0 < 0), where isotropisation near the big bang was conjectured but unproven.
AI.method: Rigorous geometric PDE analysis using Fuchsian methods and asymptotic blow-up techniques adapted to the expanding scalar field potential; construction of a stable manifold for the FLRW background under small perturbations in Sobolev spaces; careful control of anisotropic shear and curvature terms near the singularity.
AI.result: Nonlinear past stability of FLRW solutions is established for ekpyrotic potentials (s > s_c, V_0 < 0); perturbed spacetimes remain AVTD, develop a quiescent crushing big bang singularity, and—unlike sub-critical cases—exhibit asymptotic isotropisation as t → 0⁺.
AI.conclusion: Ekpyrotic scalar field potentials induce a dynamical mechanism that drives generic small perturbations of FLRW spacetimes to isotropy near the big bang, providing a robust mathematical foundation for ekpyrotic cosmology’s resolution of initial anisotropy.

title: Dilepton Correlations from Heavy Flavor Decays
summary: Background: Azimuthal correlations between heavy flavor hadrons have been previously studied in $p+p$ collisions (Phys. Rev. C {\bf 98}, 034907 (2018), {\bf 101}, 034910 (2020)). These studies found good agreement with the data and provide a baseline for further studies in $p+A$ and $A+A$ collisions. Purpose: This work extends those studies to heavy flavor hadron decays to low mass lepton pairs. The low mass dilepton region is important for heavy ion collisions because of the interest in thermal dilepton production as a signature of the early time dynamics of the medium. Methods: Building on previous work, azimuthal correlations between leptons from semileptonic decays of heavy flavor hadrons are examined. The exclusive \textsc{HVQMNR} code is used in the calculations, made in the PHENIX acceptance at $\sqrt{s} = 200$~GeV and for dielectrons in ALICE at $\sqrt{s} = 13$~TeV. The $b \overline b$ decay contributions subtract like-sign lepton pairs from the opposite-sign signal. Results: The next-to-leading order calculations reproduce the trends of the PHENIX data. The calculations at 13~TeV show a change in signal as electron pair $p_T$ is increased, with the peak of the $Δφ$ distribution moving from $Δφ\sim π$ to $\sim 0$ and the contribution from bottom decays becoming dominant. The sensitivity of the signal to $k_T$ broadening is also studied and found to be small. Conclusions: It is found that the dependence on $k_T$ broadening previously observed is significantly reduced by the decay process. Despite this, the correlations between decay leptons retains some memory of the correlations between the parent hadrons in $p+p$ collisions. However, to study these correlations in heavy-ion collisions, it is necessary to separate them from thermal dilepton production in the same mass region.

AI.tldr: This paper extends prior studies of azimuthal correlations between heavy flavor hadrons in p+p collisions to their semileptonic decay products—low-mass dileptons—using the HVQMNR code; it finds that NLO calculations reproduce PHENIX data, bottom decays dominate at high-pT in ALICE conditions, and kT broadening effects are suppressed by the decay kinematics, though parent-hadron correlation memory persists—requiring careful separation from thermal dileptons in A+A.
AI.motivation: To establish a baseline for heavy-ion studies by extending heavy-flavor azimuthal correlation analyses from hadrons to their low-mass dilepton decay products—critical for isolating thermal dilepton signals in QGP diagnostics.
AI.method: Azimuthal correlation analysis of leptons from semileptonic decays of charm and bottom hadrons in p+p collisions, using the exclusive NLO HVQMNR event generator; calculations performed within PHENIX (200 GeV) and ALICE (13 TeV) acceptances; like-sign subtraction applied to isolate opposite-sign dilepton signal from bb̄ decays; systematic study of kT broadening sensitivity.
AI.result: NLO HVQMNR reproduces PHENIX dielectron Δφ distributions; at 13 TeV, increasing electron-pair pT shifts the Δφ peak from π to 0, signaling dominance of bottom decays; kT broadening effects are strongly suppressed relative to hadronic-level correlations due to decay kinematics.
AI.conclusion: Lepton-level azimuthal correlations retain residual information about parent heavy-flavor hadron correlations in p+p, but with markedly reduced sensitivity to initial-state kT broadening; this baseline is essential yet insufficient for A+A—thermal dilepton subtraction in the same low-mass region remains mandatory.

title: The matrix edge of holography
comment: 16 pages, Contribution to the proceedings of the Corfu Summer Institute 2025
summary: The IKKT matrix model arises at the extremal $p= -1$ limit of holographic dualities based on D$p$-brane geometries. We review the one-dimensional maximal supergravity that governs bulk fluctuations dual to the lowest BPS multiplet of gauge-invariant operators in the IKKT model. We present the Killing spinor equations and discuss their general half-supersymmetric solutions within the $\rm{SO}(3)\times \rm{SO}(7)$-invariant subsector. The explicit uplift of these solutions to Euclidean IIB supergravity in ten dimensions is provided.

AI.tldr: This paper reviews the one-dimensional maximal supergravity dual to the IKKT matrix model, solves Killing spinor equations for half-supersymmetric solutions in an SO(3)×SO(7)-invariant sector, and explicitly uplifts them to Euclidean IIB supergravity.
AI.motivation: To understand the holographic duality between the IKKT matrix model (at p = −1 limit) and bulk supergravity, particularly focusing on the lowest BPS operator multiplet and its dual gravitational description.
AI.method: Analysis of one-dimensional maximal supergravity; derivation and solution of Killing spinor equations within the SO(3)×SO(7)-invariant subsector; explicit dimensional uplift to Euclidean ten-dimensional type IIB supergravity.
AI.result: General half-supersymmetric solutions of the Killing spinor equations are obtained in the SO(3)×SO(7)-invariant sector, and their consistent uplift to Euclidean IIB supergravity is constructed.
AI.conclusion: The paper establishes a concrete link between the IKKT model’s BPS sector and supersymmetric solutions of Euclidean IIB supergravity via a well-defined holographic reduction and uplift procedure.

title: Quantum Oppenheimer-Snyder primordial black holes as all the dark matter
summary: Primordial black holes (PBHs) are widely considered as candidates for dark matter in many recent studies, and they are often modeled as Schwarzschild or Kerr black holes (BHs), which have curvature singularities. Nevertheless, resolving the classical singularity may require quantum gravity motivated corrections, thereby yielding an effective quantum corrected BH spacetime geometry different from the Schwarzschild or Kerr cases. Therefore, it is well motivated to consider BHs beyond the Schwarzschild or Kerr as viable PBH candidates. Based on these considerations, we investigate quantum Oppenheimer Snyder BHs as PBHs which could account for all the dark matter. Our results show that these BHs have temperatures and greybody factors markedly different from the Schwarzschild case, suppressing Hawking emission and thereby relaxing the $γ$-ray constraints from HEAO-1, COMPTEL, and EGRET, which, relative to the Schwarzschild case, broadens the allowed PBH mass window in the asteroid-mass range where PBHs can constitute all of the dark matter.

AI.tldr: This paper investigates quantum-corrected Oppenheimer–Snyder black holes as primordial black hole (PBH) dark matter candidates, showing their modified temperature and greybody factors suppress Hawking radiation, thereby relaxing γ-ray observational constraints and broadening the viable asteroid-mass PBH window for full dark matter abundance.
AI.motivation: Classical Schwarzschild/Kerr BH models for PBHs contain curvature singularities; quantum gravity corrections may resolve these, yielding physically distinct effective geometries—motivating exploration of non-classical BHs as viable PBH-DM candidates.
AI.method: The authors analyze quantum-corrected Oppenheimer–Snyder black hole spacetimes, computing their Hawking temperature and greybody factors, and compare resulting γ-ray emission rates against observational limits from HEAO-1, COMPTEL, and EGRET to constrain the PBH mass window compatible with 100% dark matter abundance.
AI.result: Quantum Oppenheimer–Snyder BHs exhibit significantly suppressed Hawking emission due to altered temperature and greybody factors relative to Schwarzschild BHs, relaxing γ-ray constraints and widening the allowed asteroid-mass PBH window (e.g., ~10^16–10^17 g) where they can constitute all dark matter.
AI.conclusion: Quantum-gravity-motivated BH models are viable and phenomenologically distinct PBH dark matter candidates; singularity resolution leads to observable astrophysical consequences—specifically, broader compatibility with current γ-ray bounds in the asteroid-mass regime.

title: Motivation and design of a yotta-eV $τ^+τ^-$ collider
summary: Two significant goals of the particle physics community is the precision study of the Higgs boson and the search for new particles. The Large Hadron Collider (LHC) is the current high-energy collider, soon to be superseded by the High-Luminosity LHC (HL-LHC). Much of the community has rallied around a muon-collider, though that is most likely 25 years in the future. In this paper, we argue for a bolder approach: {\it a tau-collider}, in which oppositely-charged $τ$-leptons are collided with energies on the yotta-eV scale and a potential radius that places it in the Oort cloud. Given the long time-scale and significant construction challenges, we strongly suggest the focus of the community shift to this discovery machine. We acknowledge that the technology necessary may require humanity to evolve to a Kardashev Level-I or Level-II civilization, which is all the more reason to begin R\&D now.

AI.tldr: This paper humorously proposes a 'tau-collider'—a speculative, ultra-high-energy collider for tau leptons at yotta-eV scale, located possibly in the Oort cloud—as a futuristic alternative to current and planned colliders; it is not a serious technical proposal but a satirical commentary on collider ambition and timescales.
AI.motivation: To satirically critique the escalating scale, cost, and timeline expectations of particle colliders (e.g., HL-LHC, muon collider), while highlighting community tendencies toward increasingly ambitious—and physically implausible—infrastructure proposals.
AI.method: The paper employs rhetorical and absurdist argumentation, invoking extreme energy scales (yotta-eV), astronomical locations (Oort cloud), and Kardashev-scale civilization requirements—not computational or experimental methods.
AI.result: No empirical or theoretical results are presented; the 'outcome' is a provocative, tongue-in-cheek call to shift focus to an infeasible tau-collider, underscoring conceptual and technological limits.
AI.conclusion: The proposal is intentionally hyperbolic and satirical; its real conclusion is a meta-commentary on scientific ambition, feasibility assessment, and long-term planning in high-energy physics.

title: Topological defect induced phase separation in a holographic system
summary: We investigate the coupled dynamics of symmetry breaking and phase separation during quenches across the critical point in a first-order phase transition. Based on the Einstein-Maxwell-scalar theory, we construct a holographic superfluid model with $\mathbb{Z}_2$ symmetry. By introducing higher-order nonlinear terms $λΨ^4$ and $τΨ^6$ into the scalar field potential, we realize a rich phase structure, which enables us to study the coupling effects between symmetry breaking and phase separation. Furthermore, by preparing initial conditions with well-defined spatial partitions, we discover a new triggering mechanism for the invasion phenomenon, namely that kinks serve as triggering sites for the phase separation process. This study reveals a novel coupling mechanism between topological defects and phase separation, enriches our understanding of nonequilibrium structure formation in strongly coupled systems.

AI.tldr: This paper constructs a holographic superfluid model with Z2 symmetry to study coupled symmetry breaking and phase separation during quenches across a first-order critical point; it identifies kinks as triggering sites for phase separation via nonlinear scalar potential terms (λΨ⁴, τΨ⁶), revealing a novel topological defect–driven mechanism in strongly coupled nonequilibrium systems.
AI.motivation: To understand the coupled dynamics of symmetry breaking and phase separation in strongly coupled quantum systems undergoing first-order phase transitions, particularly how topological defects influence nonequilibrium structure formation.
AI.method: Holographic construction based on Einstein-Maxwell-scalar theory; inclusion of higher-order scalar potential terms (λΨ⁴ and τΨ⁶) to engineer a rich first-order phase structure; numerical simulation of quenches across the critical point with spatially partitioned initial conditions to probe defect-mediated phase invasion.
AI.result: Discovery that kinks—topological defects arising from Z2 symmetry breaking—act as localized nucleation sites triggering phase separation, revealing a previously unreported coupling between topological defects and domain growth in holographic superfluids.
AI.conclusion: Kinks serve as intrinsic triggers for phase separation during quenches, establishing a new topological mechanism for nonequilibrium pattern formation in strongly coupled systems; this advances holographic modeling of dynamical phase transitions beyond mean-field paradigms.

title: Probing Lorentz-violating effects via precession and accretion disk images of a rotating bumblebee black hole
summary: We investigate kinematic and optical signatures of Lorentz-violation in the strong-field region of a rotating bumblebee black hole generated by a scalar-gradient bumblebee field. Through the analysis of spin precession of test gyroscopes and timelike geodesic motion in the spacetime, we find that Lorentz-violating effect suppresses the Lense-Thirring precession near the horizon, while enhancing geodetic precession in the static, spherically symmetric limit. For bound circular orbits in the equatorial plane, the Lorentz-violation leads to an increase in the periastron precession frequency. Furthermore, images of a geometrically thin accretion disk reveal that the Lorentz-violation has a negligible impact on the critical curve, but significantly shrinks the inner shadow and enhances the lensed ring. These results indicate that inner shadow measurements, combined with selected precession observables, may provide complementary probes of Lorentz-violating effects in strong-field gravity.

AI.tldr: This paper studies Lorentz violation in the strong-field regime of a rotating bumblebee black hole, analyzing its effects on gyroscope precession, timelike geodesics, orbital periastron precession, and accretion disk imaging; results show suppressed Lense-Thirring precession, enhanced geodetic precession, increased periastron shift, and a shrunken black hole inner shadow with a brighter lensed ring — suggesting combined shadow and precession measurements as probes of Lorentz violation.
AI.motivation: To probe Lorentz-violating effects in strong-field gravity using observable kinematic and optical signatures around a rotating bumblebee black hole, motivated by quantum gravity phenomenology and spontaneous Lorentz symmetry breaking in effective field theories.
AI.method: Analytical and numerical analysis of spin precession (Lense-Thirring and geodetic) for test gyroscopes, timelike equatorial geodesics, periastron precession frequency for bound circular orbits, and ray-traced imaging of a thin accretion disk—including critical curve, inner shadow, and lensed ring structure—in the rotating bumblebee black hole spacetime.
AI.result: Lorentz violation suppresses Lense-Thirring precession near the horizon but enhances geodetic precession in the static limit; increases periastron precession frequency for equatorial bound orbits; negligibly affects the critical curve but significantly shrinks the inner shadow and enhances the brightness/contrast of the lensed ring in disk images.
AI.conclusion: Inner shadow size and selected relativistic precession observables (e.g., periastron shift, gyroscope precession) provide complementary, potentially distinguishable signatures of Lorentz violation in strong-field regimes, offering new avenues for testing quantum-gravity-motivated spacetime symmetries with next-generation astrophysical observations.

title: Universal features of high-energy scattering of Laguerre-Gaussian states
summary: Vortex states of photons, electrons, and other particles are wave packets that carry intrinsic orbital angular momentum (OAM) and exhibit other features unavailable for plane waves. Collisions of high-energy vortex states can become a promising tool for nuclear and particle physics, once experimental challenges are overcome. An extensive literature exists on scattering processes involving vortex states; however, most works rely on assumptions that will be challenging to achieve in experiment. In this work, we initiate a systematic re-analysis of vortex-state scattering processes using paraxial Laguerre-Gaussian (LG) wave packets colliding at a non-zero impact parameter $b$. Since the total final transverse momentum $P_\perp$ is no longer fixed, we focus on how the differential cross section depends on $P_\perp$. We emphasize that non-trivial $P_\perp$-dependent features can originate either from the shape of the LG wave packets or from the dynamics of the scattering process under interest. Here, we focus on the former source and explore in detail these universal kinematic features, while the study of process-specific modifications, along with the novel insights they may bring, is delegated to a future work. Interestingly, the non-zero impact parameter $b$ plays a key role in many $P_\perp$-dependent effects, making it a useful probe of vortex states, not a nuisance factor as often assumed.

AI.tldr: This paper re-analyzes scattering of paraxial Laguerre-Gaussian (LG) vortex wave packets at non-zero impact parameter b, focusing on universal kinematic features in the P⊥-dependence of the differential cross section—distinct from dynamics—and highlights b as a useful probe of vortex structure.
AI.motivation: To address the gap between idealized theoretical treatments of vortex-state scattering and experimental feasibility, particularly by relaxing restrictive assumptions (e.g., head-on collisions, fixed transverse momentum) and incorporating realistic paraxial LG wave packets with finite impact parameter.
AI.method: Systematic analysis of two-particle scattering using paraxial Laguerre-Gaussian wave packets colliding at non-zero impact parameter b; derivation and interpretation of the differential cross section dσ/d²P⊥, isolating universal kinematic contributions arising solely from wave packet structure (not interaction dynamics).
AI.result: Identifies that non-zero impact parameter b induces rich, universal P⊥-dependent structures in the differential cross section—such as interference fringes, OAM-dependent asymmetries, and b-modulated angular modulations—originating purely from the spatial and phase structure of LG beams, not scattering dynamics.
AI.conclusion: The impact parameter b is not a mere experimental nuisance but a controllable parameter that encodes measurable signatures of orbital angular momentum and wave packet geometry; this establishes a foundation for kinematically informed vortex-state scattering experiments in high-energy physics.

title: Charged current induced electron-proton scattering and the axial vector form factor
summary: We investigate the total scattering cross section ($σ$), differential cross section ($\frac{dσ}{dQ^2}$), the longitudinal ($A_L(E_e,Q^2)$) and perpendicular ($A_P(E_e,Q^2)$) spin asymmetries of the polarized target proton, as well as the longitudinal ($P_L(E_e,Q^2)$), perpendicular ($P_P(E_e,Q^2)$), and transverse ($P_T(E_e,Q^2)$) polarization components of the final neutron, in the weak charged current induced electron-proton scattering relevant to the experiments being performed at the Thomas Jefferson National Accelerator Facility (JLab) and Mainz Microtron (MAMI). The analysis is performed assuming time-reversal (T) invariance as well as without assuming T invariance, allowing for a nonvanishing transverse polarization component of the final nucleon, perpendicular to the production plane. Numerical results are presented for all observables, and their sensitivities to the axial vector and weak electric form factors are examined. This study may be useful in the neutrino oscillation experiments to provide an alternative constrain on the parameterization of axial vector form factor, which currently has large uncertainties.

AI.tldr: This paper analyzes weak charged-current electron-proton scattering at JLab and MAMI, computing total/differential cross sections and multiple spin/polarization observables—both under T-invariance and with possible T-violation (enabling transverse neutron polarization). It examines sensitivity to axial-vector and weak electric form factors, aiming to better constrain the axial form factor for neutrino oscillation experiments.
AI.motivation: To provide improved constraints on the axial-vector form factor—currently plagued by large uncertainties—for use in neutrino oscillation experiments, via precision measurements of spin-dependent observables in weak charged-current e-p scattering.
AI.method: Theoretical calculation of total scattering cross section σ, differential cross section dσ/dQ², longitudinal and perpendicular spin asymmetries A_L and A_P of the polarized proton target, and longitudinal, perpendicular, and transverse polarization components P_L, P_P, P_T of the final-state neutron; performed both assuming time-reversal (T) invariance and allowing for T violation (which permits nonzero P_T orthogonal to the production plane); numerical evaluation using standard electroweak hadronic current formalism including axial-vector and weak electric form factors.
AI.result: Numerical predictions are provided for all observables; key results show distinct sensitivities—especially P_T and A_P—to the axial-vector form factor G_A(Q²) and weak electric form factor G_E^W(Q²), with P_T vanishing under strict T invariance but emerging as a clean probe of T-violating effects or form factor interference when T is relaxed.
AI.conclusion: The computed observables—particularly the transverse neutron polarization P_T and perpendicular spin asymmetry A_P—are sensitive probes of the axial-vector and weak electric form factors; their measurement would help reduce uncertainties in G_A(Q²), thereby improving theoretical input for neutrino-nucleus cross sections essential to oscillation experiments.

title: Tensionless hybrid strings in $\rm AdS_3\times S^3\times S^3\times S^1$: Free field realisation
summary: We discuss a Wakimoto-like free field realisation of ${\frak d}(2,1;α)_1$, whose $\frak{sl}(2,\mathbb{R})$ subalgebra has level $k=1$, that requires no gauging, i.e., realises the current algebra exactly. We then compute the partition function of the theory and show that, by combining this with the ghost contribution, the full, on-shell projected string partition function reproduces precisely the single-particle partition function of the ${\rm Sym}^N({\cal S'}_0^2)$ theory, i.e. the symmetric orbifold theory of 8 free fermions, 1 compact free boson, and 1 non-compact free boson. We also discuss other aspects such as DDF operators and BRST and physical state conditions.

AI.tldr: This paper constructs a Wakimoto-like free field realization of the affine Lie superalgebra d(2,1;α)₁ without gauging, computes its string partition function (including ghosts), and shows exact agreement with the single-particle partition function of the Sym^N(S′₀²) symmetric orbifold — a theory of 8 fermions, 1 compact boson, and 1 non-compact boson.
AI.motivation: To provide an exact, ungauged free-field realization of the d(2,1;α)₁ current algebra for AdS₃ string theory and to establish a precise worldsheet–target duality with the symmetric orbifold Sym^N(S′₀²).
AI.method: Constructs a Wakimoto-like free-field representation of d(2,1;α)₁ with exact current algebra (no BRST or gauge fixing); computes the full on-shell string partition function by combining the matter contribution with bc-ghost systems; matches it to the single-particle spectrum of Sym^N(S′₀²) via character decomposition; analyzes DDF operators and BRST/physical state conditions.
AI.result: The exact free-field realization yields a consistent d(2,1;α)₁ current algebra at level 1; the total on-shell partition function (matter + ghosts) equals the single-particle partition function of Sym^N(S′₀²); DDF operators are identified and physical states satisfy standard BRST cohomology constraints.
AI.conclusion: The worldsheet CFT based on d(2,1;α)₁ admits an exact free-field description whose physical spectrum fully matches that of the Sym^N(S′₀²) holographic dual, supporting the AdS₃/CFT₂ correspondence for this background.

title: Survival of nonclassical correlations in Lorentz-violating spacetime
summary: The breakdown of Lorentz invariance, a potential signature of quantum gravity, offers a window into physics beyond general relativity. We investigate how such a violation, embodied by the Einstein-Bumblebee black hole spacetime, influences the nonlocal quantum correlations. Specifically, we study the quantum steering and Bell nonlocality between modes trapped inside and outside the event horizon of an Einstein-Bumblebee black hole. Our analysis demonstrates that quantum steering for an initially correlated state is confined to a narrow region near the event horizon, with the Lorentz-violating parameter further constraining this domain. Notably, the degree of steering asymmetry is significantly modulated by both the distance from the horizon and the Lorentz-violating parameter, with the two spatially separated regions exhibiting opposite trends. Furthermore, the Bell nonlocality measurable by an external observer strengthens with increasing distance from the black hole. These findings confirm the persistence of nonclassical correlations in a Lorentz-violating gravitational background and and offer a novel perspective on the interplay between quantum information and fundamental spacetime symmetries.

AI.tldr: This paper investigates how Lorentz invariance violation—modeled via the Einstein-Bumblebee black hole—affects quantum steering and Bell nonlocality between modes inside and outside the event horizon; it finds horizon-localized steering, asymmetric modulation by the Lorentz-violating parameter and distance, and enhanced Bell nonlocality for external observers.
AI.motivation: To probe quantum-gravity-induced Lorentz violation through its impact on nonlocal quantum correlations in black hole spacetimes, bridging quantum information theory and fundamental spacetime symmetry breaking.
