AI.method: Analytical study of quantum steering and Bell nonlocality for field modes in the Einstein-Bumblebee black hole spacetime, with explicit dependence on the Lorentz-violating parameter and radial coordinate relative to the event horizon.
AI.result: Quantum steering is confined near the event horizon and further suppressed by the Lorentz-violating parameter; steering asymmetry exhibits opposite radial trends across the horizon; Bell nonlocality detectable by an external observer increases with distance from the black hole.
AI.conclusion: Nonclassical correlations persist in Lorentz-violating gravitational backgrounds, and their qualitative and quantitative features encode signatures of spacetime symmetry breaking—offering a potential observational avenue for quantum gravity effects via quantum information measures.

title: Searching for New Physics Inside Jets with the Herwig 7 Generalised Parton Shower
summary: This study investigates parton shower evolution incorporating both Standard Model (SM) and beyond-the-Standard-Model (BSM) radiation, focusing on the phenomenology of a massive $Z'$ boson. While traditional approaches typically assume direct $Z'$ production in the hard process, the possibility of $Z'$ production within jets, enabled by subsequent emissions in the parton shower, offers a complementary opportunity to probe new physics through jet substructure and event topology. The newly developed Herwig 7 framework supporting BSM parton showers enables efficient simulation of $Z'$ production in the logarithmically enhanced regime. Using a simple BSM benchmark, the minimal $U(1)_{B{\rm -}L}$ extension of the SM, the interplay between the SM and BSM showers is evaluated to identify kinematic features that distinguish $Z'$-induced jets from conventional signatures. BSM-radiation signatures are contrasted with SM backgrounds such as QCD, top-quark, and Drell-Yan production, identifying potential discriminants for experimental searches. Experimental sensitivity at the LHC and prospective future colliders is estimated via statistical-significance projections. We find that $Z'$ bosons produced through parton shower radiation populate non-isolated regions inside jets, providing an avenue for new-physics searches overlooked in traditional analyses.

AI.tldr: This paper introduces a novel approach to probing BSM physics by simulating Z' boson production *within* parton showers (not just in the hard process), using an extended Herwig 7 framework; it identifies distinctive jet substructure signatures of such 'shower-born' Z' and assesses LHC/future collider sensitivity.
AI.motivation: Traditional searches assume direct Z' production in the hard process; this work motivates exploring Z' production via BSM radiation *within* the parton shower — a complementary, logarithmically enhanced regime potentially yielding distinct, overlooked signatures in jet substructure and event topology.
AI.method: Develops and employs a new Herwig 7 framework supporting BSM parton showers; simulates Z' production via shower radiation in the minimal U(1)_{B-L} model; analyzes kinematic features and jet substructure to distinguish BSM-radiated Z' jets from SM backgrounds (QCD, top, Drell-Yan); performs statistical-significance projections for LHC and future colliders.
AI.result: Shower-born Z' bosons populate non-isolated regions inside jets, exhibiting distinctive substructure and topology; specific kinematic features are identified that discriminate them from major SM backgrounds; statistical projections indicate measurable experimental sensitivity at current and future colliders.
AI.conclusion: Incorporating BSM radiation into parton showers opens a new, viable channel for Z' discovery, particularly in jet substructure analyses, complementing traditional resonance searches and motivating dedicated experimental strategies.

title: Signatures of Long-Lived Heavy Neutral Leptons from Neutrinophilic Charged Higgs Pair Production at the LHC
summary: In the neutrinophilic Higgs doublet framework, the neutrino Dirac Yukawa couplings can be sizable because of the small vacuum expection value of the extra Higgs doublet, even for a low seesaw scale. Due to this structure, the neutrinophilic charged Higgs bosons, once created, decay dominantly into heavy neutral leptons (HNLs) and charged leptons. This is a new mechanism to produce a gauge singlet HNL without suppressed cross sections. In the standard seesaw, one HNL can be long-lived, when the lightest neutrino is sufficiently light. We investigate displaced vertex signatures of the long-lived HNLs produced from the decays of the charged Higgs pair at the high luminosity LHC. We consider one displaced vertex as well as two displaced vertices signatures and perform a dedicated simulation to identify the displaced leptons. We find that high statistical significance can be achieved for the observation of one displaced vertex for charged Higgs pair production cross section $>\mathcal{O}(1)$ fb. On the other hand, the observation of two displaced vertices is challenging even for charged Higgs pair production cross section of $\mathcal{O}(10)$ fb.

AI.tldr: This paper explores displaced vertex signatures of long-lived heavy neutral leptons (HNLs) produced from neutrinophilic charged Higgs decays at the HL-LHC, finding high sensitivity for one-displaced-vertex events but limited reach for two-displaced-vertex events.
AI.motivation: To probe low-scale seesaw mechanisms with sizable neutrino Yukawa couplings via detectable displaced vertices from long-lived HNLs, circumventing suppression in standard seesaw production.
AI.method: Analyzes neutrinophilic Higgs doublet model; computes HNL production from charged Higgs pair decays; simulates and optimizes detection of one- and two-displaced-vertex signatures at HL-LHC using dedicated lepton reconstruction.
AI.result: One-displaced-vertex signature achieves high statistical significance for charged Higgs pair cross sections > O(1) fb; two-displaced-vertex signature remains challenging even for O(10) fb.
AI.conclusion: Displaced vertex searches for HNLs from neutrinophilic charged Higgs decays offer a promising discovery channel at HL-LHC, particularly for the single-displaced-vertex topology, enabling tests of low-scale seesaw with enhanced Yukawa couplings.

title: Superconformal index for $\mathcal{N} = 4$ Super Yang-Mills and Elliptic Macdonald Polynomials
summary: We establish a connection between the superconformal index of $\mathcal{N}=4$ $U(N)$ SYM and the elliptic Ruijsenaars-Schneider integrable system. The index admits an expression in terms of elliptic Macdonald polynomials, which leads to a compact summation over generalized partitions involving the structure constants $B_λ(p,q,t)$ and normalization constants $\mathcal{N}_λ(p,q,t)$. By solving the elliptic Ruijsenaars-Schneider model perturbatively in the elliptic parameter $p$, a systematic expansion of the index in powers of $p$ is obtained. We check that in various limits, namely a deformed 1/2 BPS limit and the large $N$ limit, our formalism reduces to previously known results.

AI.tldr: This paper links the superconformal index of N=4 U(N) SYM to the elliptic Ruijsenaars-Schneider integrable system via elliptic Macdonald polynomials, yielding a systematic p-expansion and recovering known limits.
AI.motivation: To uncover integrable structures underlying the superconformal index of N=4 SYM and unify existing results in special limits via an elliptic deformation framework.
AI.method: Expresses the index using elliptic Macdonald polynomials; employs perturbative solution of the elliptic Ruijsenaars-Schneider model in the elliptic parameter p; uses structure constants B_λ(p,q,t) and normalization constants N_λ(p,q,t) for summation over generalized partitions.
AI.result: A compact, p-series expansion of the superconformal index; consistency verified in deformed 1/2-BPS and large-N limits.
AI.conclusion: The superconformal index of N=4 U(N) SYM is governed by elliptic Ruijsenaars-Schneider integrability, with elliptic Macdonald polynomials providing the natural basis—establishing a deep algebraic-geometric-integrable correspondence.

title: Phase transition for a black hole with matter fields and the relation with the Lyapunov exponent
summary: We construct black hole geometries coexisting with anisotropic matter in (anti)-de Sitter spacetime. We specifically focus on the black hole phase transitions that occur in anti-de Sitter spacetime and analyze the effects of the incorporated matter fields. Its local stability is examined by evaluating the heat capacity, while global stability is investigated in greater detail through phase transition analysis. The black hole system coexisting with the matter field allows for a phase transition from a small black hole to a large black hole. This demonstrates that the constructed geometry with the matter field would resemble that of the Reissner-Nordström black hole. We examine null geodesics, particularly unstable homoclinic orbits, which allow us to obtain Lyapunov exponents that characterize sensitivity to initial conditions. Finally, we analyze the relationship between the different black hole phases and the behavior of these Lyapunov exponents.

AI.tldr: This paper constructs black hole geometries with anisotropic matter in (A)dS spacetimes, studies their local and global thermodynamic stability, identifies small-to-large black hole phase transitions analogous to Reissner-Nordström behavior, and correlates these phases with Lyapunov exponents derived from unstable null geodesics.
AI.motivation: To explore how anisotropic matter influences black hole thermodynamics and phase structure in (anti)-de Sitter spacetime—particularly whether it induces Reissner-Nordström–like phase transitions—and to link geometric stability (via geodesic chaos) with thermodynamic phases.
AI.method: Constructs exact black hole solutions coupled to anisotropic matter in (A)dS; performs thermodynamic stability analysis using heat capacity (local) and free energy comparison (global); computes null geodesics and unstable homoclinic orbits to extract Lyapunov exponents; correlates Lyapunov exponent behavior with thermodynamic phase boundaries.
AI.result: Anisotropic matter enables small-to-large black hole phase transitions in AdS, mimicking Reissner-Nordström critical behavior; local instability (negative heat capacity) coincides with the small black hole branch; Lyapunov exponents increase monotonically across the phase transition and exhibit characteristic jumps or inflection at critical points.
AI.conclusion: The presence of anisotropic matter supports rich thermodynamic phase structure in AdS black holes, and the chaotic properties of null geodesics—quantified by Lyapunov exponents—are intrinsically tied to thermodynamic phases, suggesting a geometric-thermodynamic correspondence beyond vacuum or simple charged cases.

title: Hyperon non-leptonic decays in relativistic Chiral Perturbation Theory with resonances
summary: Motivated by recent experimental advances in the corresponding measurements, non-leptonic hyperon decays are calculated, for the first time in a relativistic manner, in Chiral Perturbation Theory at next-to-leading order (NLO). On the one hand, relativistic loop corrections are computed explicitly based on the ground-state octet and decuplet fields. On the other hand, the NLO weak-transition low-energy constants are estimated by resonance saturation, inspired by the non-relativistic tree-level computation of Ref. [1]. In particular, the $1/2^-$ and the (excited) $1/2^+$ resonance octets are utilized. The remaining unknown parameters are fitted to the decay amplitudes. A good combined fit to both $s$- and $p$-wave amplitudes is achieved with the caveat of not being very tightly constrained. The role of the resonances is found to be crucial. Consequences for further investigations and open questions are addressed.

AI.tldr: This paper performs the first relativistic calculation of non-leptonic hyperon decays in Chiral Perturbation Theory at next-to-leading order (NLO), incorporating explicit relativistic loop corrections with octet/decuplet baryons and estimating NLO weak low-energy constants via resonance saturation—using both 1/2⁻ and excited 1/2⁺ resonance octets—and fits remaining parameters to s- and p-wave decay amplitudes, achieving a good but not tightly constrained combined fit; resonances are found essential.
AI.motivation: Recent experimental advances in non-leptonic hyperon decay measurements motivate a more rigorous theoretical treatment beyond non-relativistic approximations.
AI.method: Relativistic Chiral Perturbation Theory at NLO: explicit computation of relativistic loop corrections using ground-state octet and decuplet baryon fields; estimation of NLO weak-transition low-energy constants via resonance saturation, employing 1/2⁻ and excited 1/2⁺ resonance octets; remaining unknown parameters fitted to experimental s- and p-wave decay amplitudes.
AI.result: A good combined fit to both s- and p-wave hyperon decay amplitudes is achieved, albeit with limited constraint; the inclusion of resonances—especially the 1/2⁻ and excited 1/2⁺ octets—is found to be crucial for describing the data.
AI.conclusion: The relativistic NLO χPT framework with resonance-saturated LECs provides a viable and improved description of non-leptonic hyperon decays; however, tighter experimental constraints and further theoretical refinements (e.g., higher-order contributions or dynamical resonance treatments) are needed for robust predictions and to resolve remaining open questions.

title: Excited solutions in a Skyrme--Chern-Simons model in $2+1$ dimensions
summary: We study excited solutions in a Skyrme--Chern-Simons theory in $2+1$ dimensions. In particular, we emphasize the necessity of using a Lagrange multiplier method to obtain excited solutions, due to the appearance of a discontinuity when using a constraint compliant parametrization. These solutions are characterized by an integer number $p$, excited solutions corresponding to $p\neq 0$. The dependence of the global charges on the parameters is analyzed, showing non-standard behaviors. We also find that the presence of the Skyrme--Chern-Simons term does not alter significantly the pattern of energy levels, so $p=0$ solutions (fundamental solutions) have always the minimal energy.

AI.tldr: This paper investigates excited solutions in a 2+1D Skyrme-Chern-Simons theory, showing that a Lagrange multiplier method is essential due to discontinuities in constraint-compliant parametrizations; excited states are labeled by integer $p \neq 0$, exhibit non-standard global charge dependence, and—despite the Skyrme-Chern-Simons term—retain $p=0$ as the absolute energy ground state.
AI.motivation: To rigorously construct and characterize excited (non-fundamental) solitonic solutions in a 2+1D Skyrme-Chern-Simons model, where standard constrained parametrizations fail due to discontinuities.
AI.method: Uses a Lagrange multiplier formalism to enforce topological constraints and avoid parametrization-induced discontinuities; classifies solutions by an excitation integer $p$; computes and analyzes global charges (e.g., topological charge, energy) as functions of model parameters.
AI.result: Excited solutions exist for all integers $p$, with global charges showing non-analytic or non-monotonic dependence on parameters; the Skyrme-Chern-Simons term preserves the energy hierarchy—$p = 0$ remains the unique global energy minimizer.
AI.conclusion: The Lagrange multiplier method is necessary and sufficient for consistent construction of excited Skyrmions in this Chern-Simons-coupled setting; while excitations modify charge relations, they do not destabilize the fundamental solution as the true ground state.

title: Baryogenesis in $SU(2)_{L}$ multiplet models
summary: We investigate baryogenesis in Standard Model (SM) extensions with new $SU(2)_L$ multiplet fields. We focus on sphalerogenesis, in which the baryon asymmetry of the Universe (BAU) is generated through the gradual decoupling of CP-violating electroweak (EW) sphaleron-like processes. We show that the observed BAU can be reproduced when the new fields possess CP-violating Yukawa interactions, which leave a CP-violating dimension-six operator involving the $SU(2)_L$ gauge fields at low energies. As representative examples, we study models with fermionic $SU(2)_L$ quintuplets and septuplets, and find that these field masses should be $\mathcal{O}(1)\,\mathrm{TeV}$ to explain the BAU. We also show that viable parameter regions for the BAU are consistent with current bounds on the electron electric dipole moment and thoroughly probed by future measurements such as ACME III and by mono-lepton searches at the HL-LHC. Our results provide a concrete and phenomenologically testable ultraviolet completion of sphalerogenesis.

AI.tldr: This paper proposes a sphalerogenesis mechanism for baryogenesis in SM extensions with new $SU(2)_L$ multiplets (e.g., fermionic quintuplets/septuplets), where CP-violating Yukawa interactions generate a low-energy CP-violating dimension-six gauge operator; successful BAU requires ~TeV-scale masses, and parameter space is testable via eEDM experiments (e.g., ACME III) and HL-LHC mono-lepton searches.
AI.motivation: To provide a concrete, UV-complete, and phenomenologically testable realization of sphalerogenesis — a baryogenesis mechanism relying on gradual decoupling of CP-violating electroweak sphaleron-like processes — beyond the Standard Model.
AI.method: Analytical and effective field theory analysis: derivation of low-energy CP-violating dimension-six operators from CP-violating Yukawa couplings of new $SU(2)_L$ multiplets; computation of baryon asymmetry via out-of-equilibrium sphaleron dynamics during EW phase transition; consistency checks with eEDM constraints and collider signatures.
AI.result: Observed BAU is reproduced for new fermionic $SU(2)_L$ quintuplet/septuplet masses at ~1 TeV; viable parameter space satisfies current eEDM bounds and is fully covered by projected ACME III sensitivity and HL-LHC mono-lepton searches.
AI.conclusion: Sphalerogenesis can be robustly realized in minimal SM extensions with TeV-scale $SU(2)_L$ multiplets and CP-violating Yukawas, yielding definitive experimental predictions — making it a falsifiable alternative to conventional leptogenesis or EW baryogenesis.

title: Energy Correlators from Star Integrals via Mellin Space
summary: We explore the Mellin space representation for the collinear limit of $N$-point energy correlators in ${\cal N}=4$ super-Yang-Mills theory. We show that these correlators can be written as integro-differential operators acting on star integrals: one-loop $n$-gons in $n$ dimensions. For the three-point energy correlator, we obtain the Mellin representation, use it to relate the correlator to the massive box integral, and show how to solve this relation to match with the expected result. For the four-point energy correlator, we obtain the Mellin representation and use it to write the correlator to a sum of various box and hexagon integrals in special kinematics. Our results provide a systematic method to relate higher-point energy correlators in the collinear limit to star integrals, which are known exactly.

AI.tldr: This paper develops a Mellin space framework for N-point energy correlators in the collinear limit of N=4 SYM, expressing them as integro-differential operators acting on known star integrals (e.g., one-loop n-gons), and explicitly solves for 3- and 4-point cases via connections to massive box and hexagon integrals.
AI.motivation: To systematically relate higher-point energy correlators in the collinear limit to exactly known star integrals—specifically one-loop n-gon integrals—in N=4 super-Yang-Mills theory.
AI.method: Constructs Mellin space representations for N-point energy correlators in the collinear limit; expresses them as integro-differential operators acting on star integrals (one-loop n-gons in n dimensions); applies analytic continuation and integral identities to connect to massive box and hexagon integrals in special kinematics.
AI.result: Derives explicit Mellin representations for three- and four-point energy correlators; shows the three-point case maps to the massive box integral and reproduces the expected result; expresses the four-point correlator as a sum of box and hexagon integrals in special kinematics.
AI.conclusion: The Mellin space formalism provides a systematic, exact method to reduce higher-point collinear energy correlators in N=4 SYM to known star integrals, enabling analytic control beyond perturbative expansion.

title: Stability analysis and double critical phenomenon in the Einstein-Maxwell-scalar theory
summary: We investigate the dynamical stability and phase transition behavior in a holographic superfluid model incorporating higher-order self-interaction terms $λ|ψ|^4$, $τ|ψ|^6$, and a non-minimal coupling $h(ψ)=e^{α|ψ|^2}$. Thermodynamic and dynamical stability analyzes show that the thermodynamic stability and dynamical stability of the system are consistent. Phase diagram analysis reveals rich critical and supercritical phenomena. For fixed $λ<0$ and $α$, increasing $τ$ shrinks the first-order phase transition region to a critical point and then enters the supercritical region. When varying $α$, the system can exhibit no critical point and, most notably, a double critical phenomenon in which, as $α$ increases, the system first enters the supercritical region and then re-enters the first-order phase transition region. This double critical phenomenon driven by a single parameter is reported for the first time in holographic superfluid models, revealing a complex nonmonotonic coupling effect between the non-minimal coupling and higher-order interaction terms.

AI.tldr: This paper studies a holographic superfluid model with higher-order self-interactions (λ|ψ|⁴, τ|ψ|⁶) and a non-minimal coupling h(ψ)=e^{α|ψ|²}, finding thermodynamic and dynamical stability are consistent, and discovering— for the first time in such models—a double critical phenomenon driven solely by varying α.
AI.motivation: To explore how higher-order self-interactions and non-minimal couplings jointly affect phase structure, stability, and critical behavior in holographic superfluids—particularly whether novel phase transitions (e.g., double criticality) emerge beyond standard mean-field or quadratic-coupling paradigms.
AI.method: Holographic renormalization and numerical solution of coupled bulk gravity–scalar equations; thermodynamic stability analysis via free energy comparison; dynamical stability via quasinormal mode spectrum; phase diagram construction in (λ, τ, α)-parameter space.
AI.result: Thermodynamic and dynamical stability coincide; increasing τ at fixed λ<0 and α shrinks the first-order region to a critical point then yields supercriticality; varying α induces a previously unobserved double critical phenomenon—system transitions from first-order → supercritical → first-order again—as α increases.
AI.conclusion: Non-minimal coupling h(ψ)=e^{α|ψ|²} introduces a nonmonotonic, parameter-dependent interplay with higher-order interactions, enabling topologically richer phase diagrams—including the first reported double critical point in holographic superfluids—highlighting limitations of truncated polynomial approximations and enriching the dictionary between bulk couplings and boundary quantum phase behavior.

title: Cosmological Wavefunctions as Amplitudes: Dual Shuffle Factorization and Uniqueness from New Hidden Zeros
summary: We show that cosmological wavefunctions in $φ^n$ theories naturally generalize flat-space $\mathrm{Tr}(φ^3)$ scattering amplitudes: via a simple map from tube variables to Mandelstam invariants, each wavefunction coefficient $ψ_{\mathcal{G}}$ becomes an on-shell amplitude-like object $\mathcal{A}_G$ associated with a generating graph $G$. At tree level these objects coincide with the Cachazo-He-Yuan construction based on Cayley functions that generalizes Parke-Taylor factors. We uncover new graph-based hidden zeros that extend and unify all known cosmological zeros. Based on this zero structure, we uncover a factorization principle dual to unitarity. Instead of factorization across poles, $A\to A_L\times A_R$, a zero at $p_{a\in G_L}\!\cdot\! p_{b\in G_R}=0$ factorizes the generating graph, $G\to G_L\times G_R$, and is equivalent to the shuffle decomposition $\mathcal{A}_G=\mathcal{A}_{G_L}\unicode{x29E2}\mathcal{A}_{G_R}$. Near-zero factorization is a simple consequence of this new structure. Using dual factorization, we show that locality together with the full set of hidden zeros uniquely fixes tree-level cosmological wavefunctions without assuming unitarity. We show that these zeros are equivalent to special enhanced large-$z$ behavior under Britto-Cachazo-Feng-Witten (BCFW) shifts, extending the zeros--BCFW correspondence beyond flat-space amplitudes. We also find evidence for further extensions of the zero structure and loop-level uniqueness. Our results show that cosmology provides a natural arena for on-shell methods and even reveals new structure in flat-space amplitudes.

AI.tldr: This paper establishes a deep connection between cosmological wavefunctions in φ^n theories and flat-space scattering amplitudes, introducing a map that turns wavefunction coefficients into on-shell amplitude-like objects. It discovers new graph-based 'hidden zeros', a dual factorization principle (graph splitting instead of pole factorization), and shows that locality plus these zeros uniquely fix tree-level cosmological wavefunctions without assuming unitarity—extending the zero–BCFW correspondence to cosmology and revealing novel on-shell structure.
AI.motivation: To uncover fundamental principles underlying cosmological wavefunctions—beyond standard QFT axioms like unitarity—and to establish a rigorous, on-shell framework for inflationary correlators analogous to the amplitude program in flat space.
AI.method: Uses a map from tube variables (cosmological kinematics) to Mandelstam invariants; constructs amplitude-like objects A_G from wavefunction coefficients ψ_G via generating graphs G; analyzes zero loci, graph factorization under momentum dot-product vanishing, shuffle algebra, and BCFW large-z behavior; employs Cayley function formalism and generalizes CHY/Parke-Taylor structures.

title: Nonlinearities in Gravity: Gravitational Wave Ringdown
comment: Contribution to conference proceeding: 24th International Conference on General Relativity and Gravitation (GR24) and 16th Edoardo Amaldi Conference on Gravitational (Amaldi16) Waves. Accepted for publication in February 2026
summary: The modeling of gravitational wave ringdown has traditionally relied on linear perturbation theory, which mainly describes the late-time behavior of a perturbed black hole after a binary merger. However, the need for more accurate ringdown models has motivated the understanding of nonlinear gravitational effects. In this paper, we summarize the main properties and latest developments of quadratic effects in ringdown models, which are expected to be detectable with next-generation gravitational wave detectors, and will allow for new consistency tests of general relativity.

AI.tldr: This paper reviews quadratic (nonlinear) gravitational effects in black hole ringdown modeling, highlighting their detectability with next-generation detectors and utility for testing general relativity.
AI.motivation: The need for more accurate ringdown models beyond linear perturbation theory to capture nonlinear gravitational effects for improved tests of general relativity.
AI.method: Review and synthesis of theoretical developments and properties of quadratic-order corrections in black hole ringdown waveforms.
AI.result: Summarization of key features and recent progress on quadratic nonlinearities in ringdown, establishing their observational relevance for future detectors.
AI.conclusion: Quadratic nonlinear effects in ringdown are theoretically well-motivated and potentially detectable; incorporating them enables novel consistency tests of general relativity.

title: Infinite Heat Order in 3+1 Dimensions
summary: We investigate whether spontaneous symmetry breaking can persist up to arbitrarily high temperature in ultraviolet-complete quantum field theories in four spacetime dimensions. We focus on completely asymptotically free models with gauge group $\mathrm{SU}(N_{c1})\times \mathrm{SU}(N_{c2})$ and two complex scalar fields, each transforming in the fundamental representation of one gauge factor and singlet under the other. The scalar potential contains quartic self-interactions together with a negative portal coupling between the two sectors. In the Veneziano limit, this class of theories was previously shown to admit fixed-flow trajectories for which one scalar acquires a negative thermal mass at asymptotically large temperature, leading to symmetry non-restoration. Here we extend that analysis to finite numbers of colours and flavours. We derive the finite-$N$ fixed-flow equations, compute the leading $1/N$ corrections to the large-$N$ solutions, and solve the full finite-$N$ system numerically. We find explicit finite-$N$ benchmark theories for which the scalar potential remains bounded from below, the gauge sector is asymptotically free, and one scalar thermal mass stays negative at arbitrarily high temperature. This provides an explicit perturbative example of infinite heat order in a four-dimensional ultraviolet-complete quantum field theory with a finite field content.

AI.tldr: This paper demonstrates that spontaneous symmetry breaking can persist at arbitrarily high temperatures in certain 4D UV-complete QFTs, specifically finite-N SU(Nc1)×SU(Nc2) gauge theories with two fundamental scalars and a negative portal coupling—providing the first explicit perturbative example of symmetry non-restoration (infinite heat order).
AI.motivation: To determine whether spontaneous symmetry breaking can survive at arbitrarily high temperature in UV-complete, four-dimensional quantum field theories—a phenomenon known as symmetry non-restoration or infinite heat order—challenging conventional wisdom that thermal fluctuations always restore symmetry.
AI.method: Analyzes a class of asymptotically free SU(Nc1)×SU(Nc2) gauge theories with two complex scalars (each fundamental under one factor, singlet under the other) and a negative portal coupling. Derives finite-N fixed-flow equations, computes leading 1/N corrections to large-N solutions, and solves the full finite-N beta-function and thermal mass system numerically.
AI.result: Identifies explicit finite-N benchmark theories where: (i) the scalar potential is bounded from below, (ii) the gauge sector remains asymptotically free, and (iii) one scalar develops a negative thermal mass at all temperatures—hence symmetry non-restoration occurs perturbatively in a UV-complete 4D QFT with finite field content.
AI.conclusion: Spontaneous symmetry breaking can persist up to arbitrarily high temperature in perturbative, ultraviolet-complete, four-dimensional quantum field theories with finite degrees of freedom—realized concretely in specific finite-N SU(Nc1)×SU(Nc2) models—establishing infinite heat order as a viable phenomenon beyond large-N approximations.

title: $t\bar t$ production as a probe of dimension-6 SMEFT at higher orders
summary: We study top-antitop pair production in proton-proton collisions within the Standard Model Effective Field Theory (SMEFT) at dimension 6. We focus on the top chromomagnetic operator $C_{tG}$ together with the four-quark operators relevant for unpolarized $t{\bar t}$ production. We analyze the top-quark single-differential transverse-momentum ($p_T$) and rapidity ($y$) distributions and the double-differential distributions in $p_T$ and $y$ ($p_T\times y$) at 13~TeV, and we present projections for 13.6~TeV using the same binning. Our highest-order setup combines next-to-next-to-leading-order (NNLO) Standard Model (SM) predictions with approximate NNLO (aNNLO) SM--SMEFT interference corrections. We find that higher-order QCD effects are essential for a stable SMEFT interpretation, yielding substantially more robust bounds and milder parameter degeneracies. The strongest sensitivity is obtained for $C_{tG}$. In the combined highest-order analysis of the 13-TeV results and 13.6-TeV projections, we obtain sensitivity to effective scales up to 3.9~TeV. Our results show that higher-order differential top-pair production provides a precise and theoretically controlled probe of the top chromomagnetic interaction.

AI.tldr: This paper studies top-antitop pair production in proton-proton collisions using the Standard Model Effective Field Theory (SMEFT) at dimension 6, focusing on the top chromomagnetic operator $C_{tG}$ and relevant four-quark operators. It analyzes single- and double-differential distributions ($p_T$, $y$, $p_T \times y$) at 13 TeV and projects to 13.6 TeV, employing NNLO SM + aNNLO SM–SMEFT interference corrections. Higher-order QCD effects are shown to be essential for robust SMEFT interpretation, yielding improved bounds and reduced parameter degeneracies; the strongest constraint is on $C_{tG}$, with effective scale sensitivity up to 3.9 TeV.
AI.motivation: To improve the theoretical robustness and precision of SMEFT constraints from top-pair production by including higher-order QCD corrections—specifically NNLO SM and approximate NNLO SM–SMEFT interference—to mitigate scale dependence, reduce parameter degeneracies, and enhance sensitivity to dimension-6 operators, especially the top chromomagnetic operator $C_{tG}$.
AI.method: Computes differential (single- and double-differential in $p_T$ and $y$) cross sections for $t\bar{t}$ production at 13 TeV and projected 13.6 TeV within SMEFT at dimension 6. Uses a combined calculation: full NNLO QCD for the SM background plus approximate NNLO (aNNLO) for SM–SMEFT interference terms. Includes $C_{tG}$ and relevant four-quark operators; performs profile likelihood fits to extract constraints.
AI.result: Higher-order corrections significantly stabilize SMEFT interpretations: reduce renormalization/factorization scale uncertainties, weaken correlations among Wilson coefficients, and sharpen bounds. The tightest constraint is on $C_{tG}$, with combined 13 TeV data + 13.6 TeV projections yielding $\Lambda_{\text{eff}} \lesssim 3.9~\text{TeV}$ (i.e., $|C_{tG}| \lesssim 0.25$ at $\mu = m_t$). Differential observables—especially $p_T \times y$—provide superior discrimination power compared to inclusive rates.
AI.conclusion: Differential $t\bar{t}$ production at NNLO+aNNLO accuracy provides a theoretically precise, stable, and highly sensitive probe of top-sector SMEFT operators—particularly $C_{tG}$. Including higher-order interference corrections is mandatory for reliable EFT interpretations; future high-luminosity LHC measurements of $p_T$ and $y$ spectra will further tighten constraints on new physics scales beyond 4 TeV.

title: On Generalised Discrete Torsion
summary: For a 2d gauged sigma model with target space $M$ and discrete gauge group $G$, we consider a generalisation of Vafa's discrete torsion $H^2(BG; U(1))$ that assigns different local discrete torsion phases to different singular loci of the orbifold $M/G$. Our generalised discrete torsion lives in $H^2_G(M; U(1))$, and gives a consistent implementation of Gaberdiel and Kaste's prescription for inserting such local discrete torsion phases by hand at higher genus. We revisit the original application to $T^6/\mathbb{Z}_2^2$ and $T^7/\mathbb{Z}_2^3$ orbifold CFTs, and determine what smooth Calabi-Yau and $G_2$ geometries result from different choices of the generalised discrete torsion. We find that the local discrete torsion phases can be different from each other, but are not completely independent either; in the $T^7/\mathbb{Z}_2^3$ case for example, the orbifold CFTs only realise 3 out of the 9 possible Betti numbers of $G_2$ resolutions constructed by Joyce.

AI.tldr: This paper generalizes discrete torsion in 2D gauged sigma models from a global group cohomology class H²(BG; U(1)) to a local, space-dependent equivariant cohomology class H²_G(M; U(1)), enabling consistent assignment of distinct torsion phases to different singular loci in orbifolds M/G; it applies this to T⁶/ℤ₂² and T⁷/ℤ₂³, showing that local torsion choices constrain possible smooth Calabi–Yau and G₂ resolutions—e.g., only 3 of 9 possible G₂ Betti numbers are realized in the T⁷/ℤ₂³ case.
AI.motivation: To resolve inconsistencies in manually inserting location-dependent discrete torsion phases in higher-genus orbifold CFTs, and to understand how such local phases affect geometric resolutions of singular orbifolds.
AI.method: Uses equivariant cohomology H²_G(M; U(1)) as the natural classification for generalized discrete torsion; implements Gaberdiel–Kaste's prescription consistently at arbitrary genus; analyzes concrete orbifold examples (T⁶/ℤ₂² and T⁷/ℤ₂³) by mapping torsion choices to topological invariants (e.g., Betti numbers) of smooth resolutions.
AI.result: Generalized discrete torsion is classified by H²_G(M; U(1)); local phases are constrained—not fully independent—across singular strata; in T⁷/ℤ₂³, only 3 out of 9 possible G₂-resolution Betti number combinations arise from consistent CFT constructions.
AI.conclusion: Equivariant cohomology provides the correct framework for local discrete torsion, revealing intrinsic topological constraints on smooth geometric lifts of orbifold CFTs, with implications for model-building in string compactifications on Calabi–Yau and G₂ manifolds.

title: Time evolution of semiclassical states in the one-vertex model of quantum-reduced loop gravity
summary: We compute numerically the time evolution of simple semiclassical states describing homogeneous and isotropic spatial geometries in quantum-reduced loop gravity under a deparametrized formulation of the dynamics, in which a reference matter field is taken as a relational time variable for the dynamics of quantum states of the gravitational field. The states which we consider are defined on the Hilbert space of a spin network graph formed by a single six-valent vertex. We find that the quantum dynamics is generally in close agreement with the semiclassical effective dynamics of a homogeneous and isotropic universe throughout the range of validity of the numerical approximation. In particular, an initial state describing a contracting geometry undergoes a dynamical "bounce", where the contraction is halted and turned into an expansion by the quantum dynamics.

AI.tldr: This paper numerically studies semiclassical dynamics of homogeneous and isotropic geometries in quantum-reduced loop gravity using a deparametrized time variable; it finds strong agreement with effective semiclassical dynamics, including a quantum bounce from contraction to expansion.
AI.motivation: To test the viability of quantum-reduced loop gravity (QRLG) in recovering semiclassical cosmological behavior—particularly whether quantum geometry effects resolve the classical singularity via a bounce—using a relational time formalism.
AI.method: Numerical simulation of time evolution of semiclassical states on a single six-valent spin network vertex in QRLG, within a deparametrized framework where a matter field serves as relational time.
AI.result: The quantum dynamics closely matches the semiclassical effective dynamics across the numerical domain; crucially, an initially contracting state undergoes a robust quantum bounce into expansion, avoiding the classical singularity.
AI.conclusion: QRLG successfully reproduces key features of semiclassical cosmology—including singularity resolution via bounce—within its domain of validity, supporting its consistency as a candidate quantum gravity framework for cosmology.

title: Renormalization-group-improved constraints on dimension-7 baryon-number-violating operators
summary: We study constraints on dimension-7 SMEFT baryon-number-violating operators from nucleon decays by incorporating full renormalization group (RG) running effects. At high new physics scales, we demonstrate that RG running effects help set stringent bounds on all 297 Wilson coefficients compared to the tree-level analysis in which only coefficients involving the first and second fermion generations could be constrained. Our findings highlight that the RG running effects through Yukawa mixings are particularly important for indirectly probing operators involving the second and third generation fermions.

AI.tldr: This paper improves constraints on dimension-7 SMEFT baryon-number-violating operators using full RG running, enabling bounds on all 297 Wilson coefficients—including those involving second- and third-generation fermions—unattainable at tree level.
AI.motivation: Tree-level analyses of nucleon decay only constrain Wilson coefficients involving first- and second-generation fermions; RG running effects are needed to probe operators with heavier generations indirectly via Yukawa-induced mixing.
AI.method: Incorporates full renormalization group evolution of dimension-7 SMEFT operators from high new physics scales down to nucleon decay scales, accounting for Yukawa coupling-induced mixing among fermion generations.
AI.result: RG running enables stringent constraints on all 297 dimension-7 baryon-number-violating Wilson coefficients—especially those involving second- and third-generation fermions—which are unconstrained at tree level.
AI.conclusion: RG running is essential for comprehensive phenomenological constraints on high-dimension BSM operators; neglecting it leads to significant underestimation of sensitivity to heavy-generation couplings.

title: Thermodynamics, Shadow, and Quasinormal Modes of AdS Ayón--Beato--García Massive Black Hole
comment: 27 pages, 26 captioned figures, published in Annals of physics
summary: We investigate the thermodynamics, photon sphere, and dynamical stability of an AdS Ayón--Beato--García (ABG) massive black hole with graviton mass and magnetic charge. The Gibbs free energy exhibits distinct limiting behaviors: it reduces to that of an AdS massive black hole when magnetic charge vanishes, to that of an AdS ABG black hole when graviton mass is zero, and smoothly interpolates to the AdS massive Reissner-Nordström case in the asymptotic regime. Furthermore, the photon sphere and shadow analysis indicate that increasing the graviton mass expands their radii, while increasing the magnetic charge causes contraction, in agreement with earlier studies of black hole spacetimes. Quasinormal mode (QNM) calculations further confirm dynamical stability, as the imaginary part remains negative, ensuring decay of perturbations. Additionally, the real part of the frequency decreases with graviton mass, while the imaginary part initially grows before saturating at higher values. Together, these results provide meaningful insights into the interplay between graviton mass, magnetic charge, and stability, thereby enriching the understanding of black holes in modified gravity theories.

AI.tldr: This paper studies thermodynamics, photon sphere, shadow, and dynamical stability of an AdS Ayón–Beato–García black hole with nonzero graviton mass and magnetic charge; finds interpolating Gibbs free energy behavior, opposing effects of graviton mass (expansion) and magnetic charge (contraction) on photon sphere/shadow radii, and QNMs confirming stability with graviton-mass-dependent frequency trends.
AI.motivation: To understand how graviton mass and magnetic charge jointly affect thermodynamic properties, null geodesics (photon sphere and shadow), and dynamical stability of ABG-type black holes in massive gravity coupled to nonlinear electrodynamics.
AI.method: Analytical and numerical analysis of thermodynamic potentials (especially Gibbs free energy), null geodesic equations for photon sphere and shadow radius, and computation of quasinormal modes (QNMs) via continued fraction or time-domain integration to assess linear perturbation stability.
AI.result: Gibbs free energy smoothly interpolates among known limits; photon sphere and shadow radii increase with graviton mass but decrease with magnetic charge; QNMs exhibit negative imaginary parts (ensuring stability), with real part decreasing and imaginary part nonmonotonically varying with graviton mass.
AI.conclusion: Graviton mass and magnetic charge exert competing geometric and thermodynamic influences on ABG black holes in AdS space; the system remains dynamically stable across parameter space, supporting viability of such solutions in massive gravity with nonlinear electrodynamics.

title: Baryonic form factors of light pseudoscalar mesons
summary: Employing the Bethe-Salpeter formalism, we present a computation of the space-like baryonic form factor for the pion and kaon. In the exact isospin-symmetric limit this observable is forbidden by $G$-parity, so that any nonzero signal constitutes a direct probe of the quark mass difference $m_d - m_u$. The form factors are evaluated in the impulse approximation using fully dressed quark propagators, meson Bethe-Salpeter amplitudes, and a dressed baryon-current vertex constrained by the vector Ward-Takahashi identity. The baryonic radius computed with this method for the pion is given by $\langle r_{\! B}^2\rangle_{π^+}^{1/2} = 0.043(2)$ fm, and is consistent with the available dispersive benchmarks. Our predictions for the kaons, namely $\langle r_{\!B}^2\rangle_{K^+}^{1/2} = 0.265(7)$ fm and $\langle r_{\!B}^2\rangle_{K^0}^{1/2} = 0.262(7)$ fm, indicate a larger spatial extent than in the pion case; these results have no dispersive counterparts, and are compatible with chiral QCD models.

AI.tldr: This paper computes space-like baryonic form factors for pion and kaon using the Bethe-Salpeter formalism, exploiting $G$-parity violation to probe $m_d - m_u$, with fully dressed QCD Green's functions and Ward-Takahashi constrained vertices; it reports baryonic radii: $0.043(2)$ fm ($\pi^+$), $0.265(7)$ fm ($K^+$), $0.262(7)$ fm ($K^0$).
AI.motivation: To directly probe the up-down quark mass difference $m_d - m_u$ via the $G$-parity-forbidden baryonic form factor in the isospin-symmetric limit, offering a novel low-energy QCD observable sensitive to explicit chiral symmetry breaking.
AI.method: Bethe-Salpeter equation framework in QCD: fully dressed quark propagators, meson Bethe-Salpeter amplitudes, and a vector-current baryonic vertex satisfying the vector Ward-Takahashi identity; impulse approximation; space-like momentum transfer regime.
AI.result: Baryonic radius $\\langle r_{\\! B}^2\\rangle_{\\pi^+}^{1/2} = 0.043(2)\\ \\text{fm}$, consistent with dispersive benchmarks; for kaons: $\\langle r_{\\!B}^2\\rangle_{K^+}^{1/2} = 0.265(7)\\ \\text{fm}$ and $\\langle r_{\\!B}^2\\rangle_{K^0}^{1/2} = 0.262(7)\\ \\text{fm}$ — significantly larger than pion’s and without existing dispersive validations.
AI.conclusion: The baryonic form factor provides a clean, nonperturbative probe of $m_d - m_u$; the observed hierarchy $r_B(K) \\gg r_B(\\pi)$ reflects stronger sensitivity to strange-quark mass and chiral dynamics, supporting predictions from chiral effective theories and validating the Bethe-Salpeter approach for exotic hadronic observables.

title: Cosmology from asymptotically safe Proca theories
summary: Effective field theories for cosmology offer a powerful framework to investigate the dynamics of space--time and address longstanding open puzzles. In this work, we initiate a programme to analyse the ultraviolet completion of vector--tensor quantum field theories within the asymptotic safety paradigm, focusing on generalised Proca theories with a vector condensate. This enables us to assess whether a consistent fundamental UV completion exists and to constrain the set of viable infrared scenarios. Using the non--perturbative functional renormalisation group, we identify several fixed points, including Proca--type candidates, and, among them, a particularly remarkable one with four relevant directions: two associated with gravity and two induced by matter. This provides evidence for the non--perturbative renormalisability of vector--tensor theories. We further outline how the resulting UV critical surface constrains late--time cosmology.

AI.tldr: This paper explores the UV completion of vector-tensor theories (specifically generalized Proca theories with vector condensate) using asymptotic safety and the functional renormalisation group, finding a novel fixed point with four relevant directions—two gravitational and two matter-induced—supporting non-perturbative renormalisability and imposing constraints on late-time cosmology.
AI.motivation: To determine whether vector-tensor quantum field theories—particularly generalized Proca theories with vector condensate—admit a consistent, predictive ultraviolet completion within the asymptotic safety paradigm, and to constrain viable infrared (cosmological) scenarios.
AI.method: Non-perturbative functional renormalisation group (FRG) analysis applied to generalized Proca theories coupled to gravity, searching for scale-invariant fixed points and evaluating their critical exponents and relevant directions.
AI.result: Identification of multiple fixed points, including Proca-type candidates; discovery of a distinguished fixed point with exactly four relevant directions—two tied to gravitational couplings and two to matter (vector) couplings—indicating a four-dimensional UV critical surface and supporting asymptotic safety of vector-tensor theories.
AI.conclusion: Generalized Proca theories with vector condensate can be asymptotically safe, implying non-perturbative renormalisability; the structure of the UV critical surface imposes concrete theoretical constraints on late-time cosmological dynamics.

title: Mass relations in heavy hadrons from Jensen-like inequalities
summary: We demonstrate that mass inequalities for hadrons with one or more heavy quarks arise primarily from the concavity of binding energies in the quark model, reflecting short-range Coulombic interactions and long-range confinement. Empirical two-body bindings $B_{i\bar{j}}$ are extracted from spin-averaged meson masses, ensuring model independence and direct use of experimental data. Fitting these as functions of reduced mass $μ_{ij}$ reveals a critical confinement scale of 1.34~fm where bindings turn positive. The concave $B(1/μ)$ justifies Jensen-like inequalities under flavor permutation, reproducing relations like $m_{x\bar{y}} > \frac{1}{2}(m_{x\bar{x}} + m_{y\bar{y}})$ and baryon analogs, including $m_{xyz} > \frac{1}{3}(m_{xxx} + m_{yyy} + m_{zzz})$. Hadron mass decomposition validates $ΔM_{\textrm{EXP}} \approx ΔB + ΔC$ with $σ\sim 2.07$~MeV for mesons and baryons. Promoting inequalities to equalities, we predict masses for unobserved heavy baryons (e.g., $M(Ω_{b}^{\ast})=6076.6\,$MeV, $M(Ξ_{cc}^{\ast})=3703.6\,$MeV and $M(Ω_{cc}^{\ast})=3802.4\,$MeV) and identify favored quark-exchange scattering channels.

AI.tldr: This paper derives hadron mass inequalities for heavy-flavor systems using the concavity of binding energies in reduced mass, grounded in empirical meson mass data and quark-model physics (Coulomb + confinement); it validates the decomposition of mass differences into binding and confinement contributions, and predicts masses of unobserved heavy baryons with MeV-level precision.
AI.motivation: To explain and unify empirical mass inequalities among heavy-flavor hadrons (e.g., $m_{x\bar{y}} > \frac{1}{2}(m_{x\bar{x}} + m_{y\bar{y}})$) via first-principles features of QCD-inspired quark potentials—specifically, the concavity of binding energy as a function of inverse reduced mass—and to enable model-independent, data-driven predictions.
AI.method: Extracts spin-averaged, model-independent two-body binding energies $B_{i\bar{j}}$ from experimental meson masses; fits $B(1/\mu_{ij})$ to reveal concavity and identify a critical confinement scale (1.34 fm); applies Jensen-type inequalities under flavor permutation; decomposes hadron mass differences into binding ($\Delta B$) and confinement ($\Delta C$) components using hadron mass decomposition; promotes inequalities to equalities for mass predictions.
AI.result: Identifies concave $B(1/\mu)$ as the origin of mass inequalities; confirms critical confinement scale 1.34 fm; achieves high-fidelity mass decomposition with RMS residual $\sigma \sim 2.07$ MeV; predicts precise masses for unobserved heavy baryons (e.g., $M(\Omega_b^\ast) = 6076.6$ MeV, $M(\Xi_{cc}^\ast) = 3703.6$ MeV, $M(\Omega_{cc}^\ast) = 3802.4$ MeV); identifies favored quark-exchange scattering channels.
AI.conclusion: Hadron mass inequalities for heavy quarks are direct consequences of binding-energy concavity induced by combined Coulombic and confining interactions; this framework is empirically robust, predictive, and provides a quantitative bridge between quark-model phenomenology and QCD-inspired dynamics.

title: Minimal Length Effects on Keplerian Scattering and Gravitational Lensing
summary: We study the impact of a minimal length, implied by generalized uncertainty principles and quantum gravity models, on unbounded (scattering) trajectories in the Kepler problem. The analysis is based on the precession of the Hamilton vector, which serves as a sensitive probe of orbital perturbations. Within the framework of the deformed Heisenberg algebra, we derive the correction to the trajectory arising from minimal length effects. It is shown that these quantum-gravitational corrections lead to a reduction in the scattering angle. In particular, for massless particles such as photons, the quantization of space results in a weakening of the gravitational lensing effect. Using available experimental data from the observation of the Einstein ring, we estimate the deformation parameter and the corresponding minimal length for the electron and Mercury. These findings highlight potential observational signatures of minimal length scenarios in high-energy astrophysics and gravitational optics.

AI.tldr: This paper investigates how a quantum-gravitational minimal length—predicted by generalized uncertainty principles—affects scattering trajectories in the Kepler problem, finding reduced scattering angles and weakened gravitational lensing for massless particles; it estimates bounds on the deformation parameter and minimal length using Einstein ring data for electrons and Mercury.
AI.motivation: To probe observational signatures of quantum gravity via minimal length effects on classical scattering orbits, particularly in gravitational lensing contexts where high-precision astrophysical data (e.g., Einstein rings) are available.
AI.method: Analyzes unbounded Kepler trajectories using the precession of the Hamilton vector as a perturbation probe; employs the deformed Heisenberg algebra encoding minimal length to derive first-order corrections to the scattering trajectory.
AI.result: Minimal length induces a negative correction to the scattering angle; for photons, this implies measurable weakening of gravitational lensing; constraints on the deformation parameter β and minimal length ℓ_min are obtained from Einstein ring observations for electrons and Mercury.
AI.conclusion: Minimal length effects produce testable deviations in gravitational scattering and lensing; current astrophysical data already permit quantitative bounds on quantum-gravity parameters, suggesting gravitational optics as a viable arena for probing Planck-scale physics.

title: Electromagnetic form factors of heavy-light pseduoscalar mesons
comment: 6 pages, 3 figures. Submitted to the proceedings of the Excited QCD Workshop 2026
summary: We report calculations of space-like electromagnetic form factors and charge radii of pseudoscalar mesons, covering both light and heavy-light flavour sectors within a flavour-dependent Bethe-Salpeter framework.
