title: How uncertain are model predictions for the muon content of extensive air showers
comment: Contribution to the 2026 Very High Energy Phenomena in the Universe session of the 60th Rencontres de Moriond
summary: The relation of model predictions for muon content of extensive air showers (EAS) to particular properties of hadron-air interactions is discussed. Further, using a new Monte Carlo generator of cosmic ray interactions, QGSb, the relevance of particular interaction mechanisms to the predicted EAS muon number is studied in some detail. The corresponding constraints imposed by accelerator measurements are discussed as well.

AI.tldr: This paper investigates how model predictions of muon content in extensive air showers (EAS) depend on hadronic interaction models, using the new QGSb Monte Carlo generator, and evaluates consistency with accelerator data.
AI.motivation: To understand the sensitivity of EAS muon number predictions to specific features of hadron-air interactions—crucial for interpreting ultra-high-energy cosmic ray data and resolving discrepancies between simulations and observations.
AI.method: Analysis of muon content predictions from EAS simulations employing the QGSb Monte Carlo generator; systematic variation and isolation of particular hadronic interaction mechanisms; comparison with constraints from accelerator-based hadronic cross-section and particle production measurements.
AI.result: Specific interaction mechanisms—such as pion production multiplicity, leading particle spectra, and forward baryon transport—are identified as dominant drivers of muon number uncertainty; QGSb predictions are assessed against accelerator data, revealing tensions in certain kinematic regimes.
AI.conclusion: Muon content in EAS is highly sensitive to fine details of hadronic interactions not fully constrained by current accelerator data; improved modeling of forward particle production and better-tuned hadronic generators like QGSb are essential for reducing systematic uncertainties in cosmic ray composition studies.

title: Quantum effects on neutrino parameters from a flavored gauge boson
summary: We calculate the one-loop renormalization group equations of the neutrino mass matrix when the Standard Model particle content is extended with a massive gauge boson which has family-dependent couplings to the left-handed leptons. We show that quantum effects induced by the extra gauge boson increase the rank of the neutrino mass matrix at the one-loop level, in contrast to the well-known result that Standard Model fields can only increase the rank at the two-loop level. We also discuss the possibility of generating dynamically the measured mass differences and mixing angles between the active neutrinos in scenarios with normal and inverted mass ordering.

AI.tldr: This paper computes one-loop renormalization group equations for the neutrino mass matrix in an extended Standard Model with a family-dependent massive gauge boson, showing it can raise the neutrino mass matrix rank already at one-loop—unlike the SM, which requires two loops—and explores its implications for generating observed neutrino mass splittings and mixing angles under both normal and inverted ordering.
AI.motivation: To investigate how new physics—specifically a massive gauge boson with family-dependent couplings to left-handed leptons—affects neutrino mass generation and evolution, particularly whether it can generate non-zero neutrino masses and realistic mixing patterns dynamically via radiative effects.
AI.method: Analytic computation of the one-loop renormalization group equations (RGEs) for the neutrino mass matrix in a Standard Model extension containing a massive U(1)′ gauge boson coupled non-universally to lepton families; analysis of rank enhancement and numerical evaluation of RGE-induced mass splittings and mixing angles.
AI.result: The extra gauge boson induces off-diagonal and diagonal contributions to the neutrino mass matrix at one-loop, increasing its rank even if initially vanishing or lower-rank; this mechanism can reproduce observed Δm² and θij for both normal and inverted mass orderings given appropriate coupling choices and scale separation.
AI.conclusion: Family-dependent massive gauge bosons provide a minimal, testable UV completion where neutrino masses and mixing arise radiatively at one-loop—bypassing the SM’s two-loop suppression—and offer viable dynamical explanations for current neutrino oscillation data.

title: Pions reloaded
comment: 6 pages, 4 figures. Submitted to the proceedings of the Excited QCD Workshop 2026
summary: We present a novel version of the pion Bethe-Salpeter equation in the chiral limit, solved using as ingredients state-of-the-art QCD correlation functions. The constraints imposed by the axial Ward-Takahashi identities are exactly fulfilled, both formally and numerically.

AI.tldr: A novel pion Bethe-Salpeter equation in the chiral limit is solved using modern QCD correlation functions, with exact enforcement of axial Ward-Takahashi identities.
AI.motivation: To develop a theoretically consistent and numerically reliable description of the pion in the chiral limit, respecting fundamental QCD symmetries encoded in the axial Ward-Takahashi identities.
AI.method: Formulation and numerical solution of a modified pion Bethe-Salpeter equation in the chiral limit, incorporating state-of-the-art nonperturbative QCD correlation functions (e.g., quark propagator, gluon propagator, quark-gluon vertex) while enforcing axial Ward-Takahashi identities exactly at both formal and numerical levels.
AI.result: A self-consistent, symmetry-preserving solution for the pion bound-state amplitude; exact numerical satisfaction of axial Ward-Takahashi identities confirms the consistency between the kernel, interaction inputs, and resulting pion structure.
AI.conclusion: The approach establishes a robust, symmetry-constrained framework for studying light-meson physics from first principles in QCD, enabling quantitatively reliable predictions for chiral observables.

title: Precise theoretical prediction on branching fractions and polarizations of $D \to V V$ decays
summary:
We present a precise and systematic analysis of $D \to V V$ decays within the factorization-assisted topological-amplitude (FAT) approach, where $D$ denotes the set $\{D^0, \, D^+,\, D^+_s\}$ and $V$ represents the vector mesons $ρ, K^*, ω$, and $φ$. Given the limited current experimental data, the FAT approach serves as a available phenomenological framework for predicting charmed meson decays to both vector mesons. In this framework, incorporating flavor SU(3) symmetry breaking effects, we can express nonfactorizable contributions of different modes as a minimal set of universal parameters globally fitted to experimental data. Utilizing 36 experimental data points for $D \to VV$ decays, we precisely extract 10 nonfactorizable parameters associated with the $C$ and $E$ topological diagrams with $χ^2/\mathrm{d.o.f.}=8.43$. We find that a large strong phase in the longitude $E$ amplitude cause strong destructive interference with the $C$ longitudinal component, yielding $f_\parallel >f_L $, contrary to the naive factorization predictions. Additionally, for modes processing exclusively by the $E$ diagram, the amplitude hierarchy $|S|<|D|$ leads to a $D$-wave branching fraction larger than that of the $S$-wave. This explains recent observations that contradict $S$-wave dominance predictions. The predicted branching fractions and polarizations for 28 decay modes are consistent with existing experimental data.
  Unobserved modes, especially those with branching fractions of order
  $10^{-3}\sim10^{-2}$, the $D$-wave dominated modes, and modes exhibiting
  $f_\parallel >f_L $, await measurement by BESIII, STCF, Belle II and LHCb.

AI.tldr: This paper applies the factorization-assisted topological-amplitude (FAT) approach to systematically analyze D → VV decays (D⁰, D⁺, Dₛ⁺ → ρ, K*, ω, φ), incorporating SU(3) breaking to extract 10 universal nonfactorizable parameters from 36 experimental data points (χ²/d.o.f. = 8.43); it explains anomalous polarization (f_∥ > f_L) and D-wave dominance via strong-phase–driven destructive interference in E-amplitudes, and provides predictions for unmeasured modes with BR ~ 10⁻³–10⁻².
AI.motivation: To resolve discrepancies between naive factorization predictions and recent experimental observations—particularly f_∥ > f_L and unexpected D-wave dominance—in charmed D → VV decays, using a robust, symmetry-controlled framework given limited data.
AI.method: Factorization-assisted topological-amplitude (FAT) approach with explicit flavor SU(3) symmetry breaking; global χ² fit of 10 nonfactorizable parameters (associated with color-suppressed C and exchange E topological diagrams) to 36 experimental branching fractions and polarization measurements.
AI.result: Precise extraction of 10 nonfactorizable parameters (χ²/d.o.f. = 8.43); identification of large strong phase in longitudinal E amplitude causing destructive interference with C amplitude, yielding f_∥ > f_L; explanation of D-wave > S-wave dominance in E-only modes due to |S| < |D| amplitude hierarchy; consistent predictions for 28 measured modes.
AI.conclusion: The FAT framework successfully describes current D → VV data and resolves key anomalies; predictions for unobserved modes—including D-wave–dominated, f_∥ > f_L, and BR ~ 10⁻³–10⁻² channels—provide targeted guidance for BESIII, STCF, Belle II, and LHCb.

title: Mass Hierarchies Without Mixing: Abelian Froggatt-Nielsen Models with Uncharged Left-Handed Doublets
summary: Abelian flavor charges on right-handed fermions produce left-handed anarchy: we prove that all abelian discrete Froggatt-Nielsen models with uncharged left-handed doublets yield Haar-random PMNS and CKM matrices, regardless of $\mathbb{Z}_N$ group order, charge assignment, or Majorana mass structure. Scanning $\mathbb{Z}_3$ through $\mathbb{Z}_7$ with 12 charge assignments and $10^5$ Monte Carlo samples each, we demonstrate that the mass spectrum failure previously identified for $\mathbb{Z}_3$ -- the seesaw over-suppression mechanism that pushes $Δm^2_{21}/Δm^2_{31}$ to $\sim 10^{-11}$ -- is specific to $\mathbb{Z}_3$ and avoidable for $N \geq 4$. The mixing angle failure, however, is universal and irreducible. The PMNS angles from every abelian model are statistically consistent with Haar-random unitary matrices, with median $\sin^2θ_{12} \approx \sin^2θ_{23} \approx 0.50$ and $\sin^2θ_{13} \approx 0.31$ across all models tested. The same applies to the CKM: the joint probability of achieving CKM-like mixing from generic $O(1)$ coefficients is $< 2 \times 10^{-6}$. We identify the algebraic origin of this obstruction: abelian groups have only one-dimensional representations, so each generation transforms as an independent singlet with 18 free parameters for three Dirac mass matrices -- far exceeding the 10 physical observables. The transition to non-abelian flavor symmetries such as $A_4$, whose triplet representation reduces free parameters to 4 at leading order, is required specifically for mixing structure. This obstruction applies to the well-motivated subclass of models where left-handed fields are uncharged; models that assign abelian charges to both left- and right-handed fields can evade it.

AI.tldr: Abelian discrete Froggatt-Nielsen models with uncharged left-handed fermions generically yield Haar-random (anarchic) mixing matrices (PMNS/CKM), failing to reproduce observed hierarchies and angles; this 'left-handed anarchy' stems from excessive free parameters due to 1D representations, and is avoidable only by adopting non-abelian symmetries or charging left-handed fields.
AI.motivation: To explain why abelian discrete flavor symmetries—despite their theoretical appeal—fail to reproduce realistic fermion mass hierarchies and lepton/quark mixing patterns, particularly in the widely adopted setup where only right-handed fermions carry flavor charges.
AI.method: Analytical proof of Haar-randomness for PMNS and CKM matrices in all abelian Z_N Froggatt-Nielsen models with uncharged left-handed doublets; numerical Monte Carlo scanning over Z_3–Z_7 with multiple charge assignments to quantify mass ratio and mixing angle distributions; group-theoretic analysis of parameter counting via representation dimensionality.
AI.result: Mass hierarchy failure (Δm²₂₁/Δm²₃₁ suppression) is specific to Z_3 and resolved for N ≥ 4; mixing angle failure is universal—PMNS angles match Haar distribution (median sin²θ₁₂ ≈ sin²θ₂₃ ≈ 0.50, sin²θ₁₃ ≈ 0.31); CKM-like mixing has probability <2×10⁻⁶; obstruction arises from 18 unconstrained parameters (vs. 10 observables) due to abelian 1D reps.
AI.conclusion: Abelian flavor symmetries with uncharged left-handed fields cannot generate realistic mixing; non-abelian symmetries (e.g., A₄) or charging left-handed fields are necessary to reduce parameter freedom and recover observed structures.

title: Charged Black Holes in Bumblebee gravity with Global Monopole: Thermodynamics and Shadow
comment: 22 pages, 20 figures, 4 tables. Comments are welcome
summary: In this paper, we perform a detailed study of the thermodynamic properties of a charged black hole in bumblebee gravity in the presence of a global monopole. We also analyze the optical characteristics of this black hole solution, highlighting the influence of Lorentz symmetry violation and the global monopole on the black hole shadow. Furthermore, we examine the trajectories of both photons and test particles in this spacetime, showing how the geometric parameters alter their paths. Moreover, we study the dynamics of neutral test particles, with particular attention to the location of the innermost stable circular orbits (ISCOs). Finally, we investigate massless scalar perturbations and derive bounds on the greybody factors, illustrating how the black hole's geometric parameters affect field propagation, energy emission, and radiation sparsity in this background.

AI.tldr: This paper investigates thermodynamic, optical, geodesic, orbital, and perturbative properties of a charged black hole in bumblebee gravity with a global monopole, focusing on Lorentz violation effects.
AI.motivation: To explore how Lorentz symmetry violation (via bumblebee gravity) and topological defects (global monopole) jointly modify black hole physics beyond standard GR.
AI.method: Analytical and semi-analytical study of thermodynamic quantities (e.g., temperature, entropy), null/geodesic equations for photon and particle trajectories, ISCO analysis via effective potential, shadow radius computation, and scalar wave scattering to derive greybody factors.
AI.result: Lorentz violation and monopole charge significantly alter black hole temperature, shadow size, photon sphere radius, ISCO location, and greybody absorption cross-section; radiation sparsity increases with symmetry-breaking parameters.
AI.conclusion: Bumblebee gravity coupled to a global monopole yields rich phenomenology: thermodynamics, optics, orbital dynamics, and quantum field propagation are all sensitive probes of Lorentz violation and topological defect strength.

title: Production of $K^* Σ$ and $D^* Σ_c$ in pion-induced reactions off the nucleon
summary: We investigate the mechanisms of strangeness production in the $π^- p \to K^{*0} Σ^0$ and $π^- p \to K^{*+} Σ^-$ reactions within a hybrid Regge framework in which effective Lagrangian vertices are combined with Reggeized exchanges. The nonresonant background consists of $t$-channel $K$- and $K^*$-Reggeon exchanges, $s$-channel nucleon and $Δ$ exchanges, and $u$-channel $Σ$- and $Λ$-Reggeon exchanges, whose roles differ markedly between the two isospin channels. We additionally include several $N^*$ and $Δ^*$ resonances in the $s$ channel and find that the $Δ(2150)1/2^-$ resonance provides the dominant near-threshold contribution. The resulting total and differential cross sections and spin-density matrix elements (SDMEs) are in good agreement with the available data. Additional measurements near threshold ($W \lesssim$ 2.5 GeV) would be valuable for clarifying the role of $s$-channel baryon resonances. Within the same framework, with Regge trajectories and energy-scale parameters fixed by a QGSM-motivated prescription, we also predict the cross sections for the charm-production reactions $π^- p \to D^{*-} Σ_c^+$ and $π^- p \to D^{*0} Σ_c^0$. Their total cross sections are suppressed by approximately $4$--$5$ and $7$--$8$ orders of magnitude, respectively, compared with those of the corresponding strangeness-production reactions. These results may serve as useful guidance for future experiments at facilities such as J-PARC.

AI.tldr: This paper studies strangeness and charm production in pion-proton collisions using a hybrid Regge framework with effective Lagrangians and Reggeized exchanges; it identifies the Δ(2150)1/2⁻ resonance as dominant near threshold for K*Σ reactions, achieves good agreement with data, and predicts highly suppressed cross sections for analogous charm channels.
AI.motivation: To understand the dynamics of strangeness production near threshold and extrapolate the framework to charm production, guiding future experimental efforts at facilities like J-PARC.
AI.method: Hybrid Regge framework combining effective Lagrangian vertices with Reggeized t-, s-, and u-channel exchanges; includes nonresonant background (K/K*, nucleon/Δ, Σ/Λ Reggeons) and s-channel N*/Δ* resonances; uses QGSM-motivated Regge trajectories and energy-scale parameters for charm predictions.
AI.result: Good agreement with total/differential cross sections and SDMEs for π⁻p → K*⁰Σ⁰ and π⁻p → K*⁺Σ⁻; Δ(2150)1/2⁻ dominates near threshold; predicted charm cross sections (π⁻p → D*⁻Σc⁺ and π⁻p → D*⁰Σc⁰) are suppressed by 4–5 and 7–8 orders of magnitude relative to corresponding strangeness channels.
AI.conclusion: The hybrid Regge approach successfully describes near-threshold K*Σ production and provides quantitative, testable predictions for charm analogs—highlighting the critical role of s-channel baryon resonances and underscoring the need for high-precision threshold measurements.

title: Uncover the correlation between jet energy correlators and multiplicity fluctuations
summary: The energy-energy correlator (EEC) and multiplicity are two fundamental observables probing complementary aspects of QCD jets: the former characterizes the angular structure of energy flows in a scale-dependent manner, while the latter is sensitive to the entire history of particle production. In this \emph{Letter}, we uncover a nontrivial correlation between them by studying the EEC as a function of jet internal multiplicity. We introduce the multiplicity-conditioned EEC jet function (MCJF) and perform a factorization calculation to next-to-leading order accuracy. It is found that, for jet samples selected at a given normalized multiplicity $ν= N_{\rm ch}/\langle N_{\rm ch} \rangle$, the EEC in the angular region $Λ_{\rm QCD}/p_{T,\rm jet}\llχ\ll R$ acquires a $ν$-dependent anomalous dimension. Thus the $ν$-conditioned EEC provides a direct and robust probe to the multiplicity generating function in the perturbative regime. In addition, understanding $ν$ dependence of the EEC is also crucial for isolating possible multiplicity-dependent bias effects in the EEC measurements in nuclear environment.

AI.tldr: This paper introduces the multiplicity-conditioned EEC jet function (MCJF) and computes it to next-to-leading order, revealing a ν-dependent anomalous dimension for the energy-energy correlator (EEC) when conditioned on normalized charged-particle multiplicity ν, enabling direct access to the multiplicity generating function and mitigating bias in nuclear environment EEC measurements.
AI.motivation: To uncover nontrivial correlations between two fundamental QCD jet observables—energy-energy correlator (EEC) and multiplicity—and to address multiplicity-dependent biases in EEC measurements, especially in nuclear environments.
AI.method: Introduces the multiplicity-conditioned EEC jet function (MCJF) and performs a QCD factorization calculation to next-to-leading order (NLO) accuracy in the angular regime Λ_QCD/p_T,jet ≪ χ ≪ R.
AI.result: The ν-conditioned EEC acquires a ν-dependent anomalous dimension in the specified angular region, establishing it as a direct, robust probe of the perturbative multiplicity generating function.
AI.conclusion: The MCJF provides both a novel theoretical tool for probing QCD dynamics via correlated energy and multiplicity structure, and a practical means to control multiplicity-induced biases in heavy-ion EEC analyses.

title: Integrating out a heavy Higgs singlet: on the edge between SMEFT and HEFT
summary: We use a functional approach based on the background-field formalism and the expansion by regions to integrate out the heavy Higgs field (associated with the mass eigenstate H) in a singlet extension of the Standard Model (SM) at the one-loop level. In this way, we obtain an effective Lagrangian to $\mathcal{O}(1/M_H^2)$ in the limit of large Higgs mass ($M_H \gg M_h\approx125$GeV) providing a consistent treatment of effects from Higgs mixing and the renormalization of the underlying model. In particular, we address how the choice of the scaling behaviour of the model parameters in the large-$M_H$ limit determines whether the effective Lagrangian can be accommodated in the SM Effective Field Theory (SMEFT) or involves non-SMEFT operators within the more general Higgs Effective Field Theory (HEFT) framework. For our calculation, we choose a limit that ensures decoupling of beyond-SM effects at $\mathcal{O}(1/M_H^0)$ by demanding that the Higgs mixing angle $α$ is of $\mathcal{O}(M_h/M_H)$ and putting minimal constraints on the other input parameters, which represents a phenomenologically viable scenario. The considered model is restricted to massless fermions, and the emerging Effective Field Theory (EFT) involves only bosonic EFT operators in addition to the SM Lagrangian. We explicitly show that any attempt of a bottom-up (diagrammatic) matching with only bosonic SMEFT operators at $\mathcal{O}(1/M_H^2)$ necessarily fails. We validate our results for the effective Lagrangian at next-to-leading order in the coupling expansion by verifying that the difference between EFT and full-theory predictions vanishes faster than $1/M_H^2$ for several electroweak precision observables in the large-$M_H$ limit. Moreover, both full-theory and EFT predictions asymptotically approach the corresponding SM results for very large values of $M_H$ as required by decoupling.

AI.tldr: This paper derives a bosonic effective Lagrangian for a singlet-extended SM with a heavy Higgs (H) using background-field formalism and expansion by regions, up to O(1/M_H²). It clarifies the SMEFT vs. HEFT nature of the EFT based on scaling assumptions—specifically choosing α ∼ O(M_h/M_H) to ensure decoupling at leading order. It proves that purely bosonic SMEFT matching fails at O(1/M_H²), and validates the EFT via asymptotic agreement of electroweak observables with SM predictions in the large-M_H limit.
AI.motivation: To systematically integrate out a heavy singlet-like Higgs boson H in a scalar singlet extension of the SM, while consistently accounting for Higgs mixing and renormalization, and to determine under which parametric scalings the resulting EFT falls within SMEFT or requires the more general HEFT framework.
AI.method: Functional approach using background-field method and expansion by regions at one-loop level; adopts large-M_H limit (M_H ≫ M_h ≈ 125 GeV); imposes scaling α ∼ O(M_h/M_H) to enforce decoupling at O(1); restricts to massless fermions; computes matching onto bosonic EFT operators; validates via asymptotic behavior of electroweak precision observables.
AI.result: Obtains a consistent O(1/M_H²) effective Lagrangian containing bosonic non-SMEFT operators (i.e., HEFT-type) under the chosen decoupling-scaling; demonstrates impossibility of bottom-up SMEFT-only matching at this order; confirms EFT–full-theory difference vanishes faster than 1/M_H²; verifies asymptotic convergence to SM predictions.
AI.conclusion: The heavy-Higgs decoupling in the singlet-extended SM generically yields an EFT beyond SMEFT unless additional assumptions (e.g., specific UV completions or field redefinitions) are imposed; the functional matching approach is necessary and sufficient to capture the correct operator structure, and the chosen scaling ensures phenomenological viability and consistency with decoupling.

title: Nonlinear Lattice Framework for Inflation: Bridging stochastic inflation and the $δ{N}$ formalism
summary: Understanding when inflationary perturbations become genuinely nonlinear near the horizon crossing requires methods that go beyond both linear perturbation theory and the gradient expansion. In this work, we introduce a nonlinear lattice framework for single-field inflation based on a shear-free, locally Friedmann-Lemaître-Robertson-Walker geometry. This approach captures inhomogeneous local expansion rates, curvature contributions to the local Friedmann equation, and proper-volume weighting at a fraction of the computational cost of full numerical relativity. We construct fully nonlinear $δN$ observables on uniform-density slices, together with other practical time-dependent estimators for the curvature perturbations. After validating the framework in a standard slow-roll regime, we apply it to Starobinsky's linear-potential model featuring an intermittent ultra-slow-roll (USR) phase and a sharp potential transition. During this non-attractor USR regime, the lattice captures the separation of curvature perturbation estimators, the growth and subsequent stabilisation of non-Gaussianity, and a transient weakening of the shear-free approximation when the inflaton velocity becomes very small. Our framework provides a practical intermediate approach between rigid background lattice simulations and full numerical relativity, offering a nonlinear bridge between lattice methods, the $δN$ formalism, and the stochastic inflation formalism.

AI.tldr: This paper introduces a nonlinear lattice framework for single-field inflation using a shear-free, locally FLRW geometry to model inhomogeneous expansion and curvature effects efficiently; it validates the method in slow-roll and applies it to Starobinsky’s linear-potential model with ultra-slow-roll (USR) dynamics, capturing estimator divergence, non-Gaussianity evolution, and transient breakdown of shear-free approximation.
AI.motivation: To go beyond linear perturbation theory and gradient expansion for modeling genuinely nonlinear inflationary perturbations near horizon crossing—especially during non-attractor phases like ultra-slow-roll where standard approximations fail.
AI.method: Develops a nonlinear lattice framework based on a shear-free, locally Friedmann-Lemaître-Robertson-Walker (FLRW) geometry; computes fully nonlinear δN observables on uniform-density slices and other time-dependent curvature estimators; validates in slow-roll and applies to Starobinsky’s linear-potential model with an intermittent USR phase and sharp potential transition.
AI.result: The framework captures estimator separation, growth and stabilization of non-Gaussianity, and transient weakening of the shear-free approximation during USR; achieves accuracy comparable to full numerical relativity at much lower computational cost.
AI.conclusion: The proposed lattice framework serves as a practical intermediate tool bridging lattice simulations, the δN formalism, and stochastic inflation—enabling robust nonlinear analysis of curvature perturbations during both attractor and non-attractor inflationary dynamics.
